picks.title: Dark matter constraints from small-scale cosmic structure
picks.abstract: Small-scale cosmic structure provides a powerful test of the fundamental nature of dark matter. A wide range of dark matter models impact matter clustering on small scales, including warm, fuzzy, and (self-)interacting dark matter. In these scenarios, dark matter physics such as free-streaming, wave interference, and self/Standard Model interactions alter the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos. Cosmological and astrophysical probes of small-scale structure—including dwarf galaxies, strong lensing, the Lyman- α forest, stellar streams, and high-redshift galaxies—are therefore sensitive to these effects. Here, we review dark matter constraints provided by small-scale structure, focusing on observables that probe scales smaller than ∼ 1 M p c , which define the frontier of current measurements. We summarize how these constraints have been translated to limits on microphysical dark matter models, and we discuss key modeling uncertainties and observational systematics. Finally, we highlight the growing importance of probe combination and simulation-based inference for this field, and we overview upcoming observational facilities that will sharpen small-scale structure tests of dark matter physics.

picks.title: Field-level Inference from Galaxies: Baryon Acoustic Oscillation Reconstruction
picks.abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) underpin the key cosmological results from modern spectroscopic galaxy surveys, but nonlinear gravitational evolution limits the precision achievable with traditional analysis methods. To overcome this, we develop field-level inference for BAO, first reconstructing the initial linear density field and then fitting the BAO signal therein. We benchmark three reconstruction methods: (i) traditional reconstruction based on linear theory, (ii) explicit field-level inference using differentiable forward modeling with hybrid effective field theory, and (iii) implicit field-level inference using a convolutional neural network to augment traditional reconstruction. Using DESI-like luminous red galaxy (LRG) and Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS) catalogs, we find that field-level approaches significantly sharpen the BAO feature relative to traditional reconstruction. For LRGs, explicit field-level inference improves constraints on the BAO scale parameters ( α iso , α ap ) by 23%–26%, while implicit inference improves constraints by 33%–34%, corresponding to a 2.2× improvement in figure of merit (FoM). For the higher-density, lower-redshift BGS sample, field-level inference enables information extraction from smaller scales, yielding an improvement in constraints of up to 46%, corresponding to a 3.2× improvement in FoM. Crucially, we address longstanding concerns regarding the robustness of field-level reconstruction by leveraging 1000 mock realizations to perform extensive coverage tests. Our results are both unbiased and statistically well calibrated, maintaining nominal coverage even when using tight simulation-informed priors and under model misspecification.

picks.title: Direct wave is not a meaningful test of horizon properties
picks.abstract: Recently, a distinct component of black hole binary merger radiation, named the direct wave, has been identified. The frequency and damping time of the direct wave have been associated with properties of the remnant horizon. This has led to direct wave based analysis of GW250114, including a test of Hawking’s area law. However, as we demonstrate here for comparable mass binaries using numerical relativity strain data, the direct wave frequency is not correlated with the horizon frequency or surface gravity, other than an incidental crossing around χ f ≈ 0.7 corresponding closely to the remnant spin of GW250114. Because the damping time shows significant evolution a single damped sinusoid model with a fixed damping time is not appropriate to model the entire direct wave, except for short time intervals. We further show that an evolving frequency model based on horizon properties also does not model the direct wave component for systems with large remnant spins. We demonstrate that testing Hawking’s area law with a horizon frequency based on the direct wave interpretation may lead to apparent violations of Hawking’s area law when no violation actually occurs. Our results therefore indicate that the direct wave is not a reliable probe of the remnant horizon’s properties for comparable mass mergers.

picks.title: Highly Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Achieving high crystallinity in three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly beyond 4-connected tetrahedral nodes toward higher-connectivity building units. Here, we report the rapid synthesis of three highly crystalline triptycene-based COFs (COF-563, −564, and −565) as well-faceted, micrometer-sized crystals under mild conditions within 24 h. By employing rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic triptycene-based building units, hexakis(4-aminophenyl/4-formylphenyl)triptycene (Trip-NH2/Trip-CHO), we access a topological regime of three-dimensional (3D) COFs that includes the established hea and stp nets as well as an unprecedented (6,6)-connected htp topology. These frameworks are constructed through reticulation of the triptycene nodes with tetrahedral (tetra(4-anilyl)methane (TAM)), rectangular (pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetraaniline (PyTTA)), and hexagonal (hexakis(4′-formyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)benzene (HFBB)) complementary linkers to yield the hea, stp, and htp structures, respectively. The resulting materials exhibit permanent porosity with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface areas of up to 3769 m2 g–1─approaching a 2-fold increase over previously reported values for related topologies─and thermal stability up to 500 °C. This work establishes a versatile platform for the rapid formation of highly crystalline 3D organic frameworks and provides a blueprint for designing complex, highly porous architectures with controlled topology.

picks.title: Turnovers Drive Supported Metal Nanoparticle Catalyst Surface Reconstruction to Kinetically Trapped Metastable Structures
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Supported metal catalysts often operate with high adsorbate coverages that can alter nanoparticle structures as compared to the clean catalyst. Such restructuring is typically described within an equilibrium picture that assumes that nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages adopt their thermodynamically preferred state. Here, we challenge this assumption and propose that under conditions of high adsorbate coverage and fast turnovers of surface species, supported metal nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages can become kinetically trapped in metastable states. We studied CO adsorption–desorption quasi-equilibrium on Pt/γ-Al2O3 using in situ IR spectroscopy and chemisorption as a function of temperature (300–650 K), CO pressure (10–2–10–4 bar), and visible photon flux (0–2 W cm–2 440 nm photons). The adsorbed CO IR band area increases with temperature and photon flux, contrary to equilibrium predictions of decreasing coverage. Estimates of apparent Pt dispersion and CO desorption rates, along with the reversibility of IR spectral changes, support the hypothesis that when CO turnovers are faster than Pt atomic rearrangements to their equilibrium state, the catalyst is driven into metastable states. We estimate atomic rearrangements time scales of 10–1–10–3 s on CO-covered Pt nanoparticles at ∼500–600 K. Grand-canonical sampling calculations show that equilibrium Pt–CO structures cannot reproduce the experimental IR trends, implying the presence of off-equilibrium coverages, structures, or both. By matching the experimental trend, theory identifies a plausible flat, nonequilibrium free-energy region that can facilitate kinetic trapping of metastable catalyst states. These results highlight the need for theoretical and experimental approaches targeting…

picks.title: The Milky Way Joins the Extragalactic World. I. PHANGS
picks.abstract: Complete catalogs of molecular clouds in the Milky Way allow analysis of the molecular medium and the star formation properties of the Milky Way that closely follows the method used for nearby galaxies, in particular in the PHANGS project. The dependencies of the depletion time on other properties of molecular gas in the Milky Way are similar to those of other galaxies when analyzed in an analogous way. They exhibit a large scatter and relatively weak correlations. The strongest correlation is a decrease in depletion time with increasing velocity dispersion. We explore the effects of spatial resolution, sensitivity, cloud identificaton method, averaging method, and tracer choice on our results. Metallicity effects in converting observations to mass can have a substantial impact. Somewhat fortuitously, differences in conversion methods between PHANGS and the Milky Way do not affect the current comparison. Inadequate spatial resolution, resulting in unresolved cloud structure, has the most important effect on the interpretation of both extragalactic observations and existing catalogs of Milky Way clouds.

picks.title: Cycles of discourse, speech dysfluency, and active inference.
picks.abstract: Speech is a complex motor and social act. We must not only produce and understand sequences of variable-length words formed from ordered syllables but also speak and listen in turn. This theoretical article introduces a computational model of speech production and auditory segmentation based on sequences of discrete phonemes . The purpose of this model is to develop a vehicle for testing (in silico) hypotheses about the mechanisms that govern the loss of speech fluency , something may occur transiently in people who stutter or progressively in various neurodegenerative conditions. The modeling presented here employs Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes that provide a useful generic formulation for specifying the internal model that our brains might use to describe dynamic environments in which they can exert partial control and make partial observations. The core features of the specific model used here are as follows: (a) a reciprocal mapping from words to sequences of varying numbers of phonemes and (b) a common subset of states for both speech generation and speech perception . A further novel feature is a social component in which one must infer who is speaking (oneself or another person). We propose a series of hypotheses about the computational mechanisms that might underwrite speech breakdown. For example, we demonstrate that reducing the precision in the next word introduces pauses and start-of-word repetitions of the sort associated with stuttering . We examine the patterns of behavior and belief-updating predicted by each of these hypotheses, with implications for both speaking and listening . Finally, we discuss plausible neural substrates for the underlying message passing that might be amenable to interrogation with functional imaging.

picks.title: Promises and pitfalls of community moderation on social media
picks.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
picks.abstract: Social media platforms have traditionally relied on internal moderation teams and partnerships with independent fact-checking organizations to identify and flag problematic content. Recently, however, platforms including X (formerly Twitter) and Meta have shifted toward community-driven content moderation by launching their own versions of crowd-sourced fact-checking—Community Notes. If effectively scaled and governed, such crowd-checking initiatives have the potential to combat misinformation as successfully as community-driven efforts once did with spam. However, moderating misinformation is inherently more complex: perceptions of truth are often shaped by personal biases, political leanings, and cultural contexts, complicating consensus on what constitutes misleading content. This suggests that community efforts, while valuable, cannot replace the indispensable role of professional fact-checkers. Here we explore the emerging role of community-driven moderation, critically evaluate both the promises and the challenges of Community Notes at scale, and identify how collaborative and technical innovations can integrate the two distinct approaches.

fig.label: Figure 1
fig.caption: An overview of the community-driven content moderation framework as proposed by major social media platforms like X, Meta, and TikTok. The moderation process is divided into two main stages: (i) Pre-Moderation using AI classifiers, which categorize content as either restricted — blocked from appearing on the platform — or less harmful , which is passed on for community moderation; and (ii) Community Moderation , where eligible volunteers may propose additional context that undergoes peer review by other contributors with diverse perspectives before being published after a consensus is achieved.

picks.title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia
picks.abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport-0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III-independent reverse-topology budding.

picks.title: How Sociotropic Aesthetic Judgments Drive Opposition to Dense Housing Development
picks.abstract: Voter opposition to dense housing development contributes to America’s housing shortage. Prevailing explanations emphasize homeowner self-interest and “NIMBYism.” We develop a theory of how sociotropic aesthetic judgments shape housing policy preferences and demonstrate its unique implications with a series of descriptive studies and experiments. First, people who choose to live in dense neighborhoods have an aesthetic taste for density, leading homeowners in already-dense areas to be more supportive of dense development both in their neighborhoods and elsewhere. Second, voters are more supportive of dense development when it is proposed in already-dense neighborhoods where it “fits”—even voters who live in those same dense neighborhoods. Finally, genuine aesthetic distaste for tall buildings is widespread and causally affects support for development. Our findings offer a new lens for understanding housing policy preferences and suggest novel solutions for addressing America’s housing shortage.

more.title: Diffusive Dynamics of Nonstabilizerness
more.abstract: Symmetries shape the quantum-information dynamics of many-body systems, but their effect on nonstabilizerness, the resource complementary to entanglement, is less understood. We compute the stabilizer Renyi entropy, a measure of nonstabilizerness, in U(1)-symmetric one-dimensional random circuits. The disorder-averaged dynamics is captured by a four-replica tensor network, which we evaluate by S4-adapted infinite time-evolving block decimation (iTEBD) directly in the thermodynamic limit. Together with a hydrodynamic argument, our results identify a diffusive universality class for the late-time approach of nonstabilizerness to its random-state value, with the stabilizer Renyi entropy gap closing as 1/t. The same scaling is verified in an energy-conserving nonintegrable Ising chain. More broadly, our framework provides a hydrodynamic perspective on nonstabilizerness generation and offers insight into the design of approximate Haar-random states in Hamiltonian dynamics.

more.title: Assembling extensive quantum Fisher information in stabilizer systems
more.abstract: We introduce a systematic framework to construct nonlocal observables with extensive quantum Fisher information (QFI) density in stabilizer codes. The construction maps stabilizer generators to dual Ising spins whose correlators equal string order parameters, converting hidden nonlocal order into a possibly metrologically accessible observable. Applying this to monitored cluster codes and the toric code, we identify transitions in the QFI scaling from an extensive regime—where long-range string order prevails—to an intensive one driven by competing single-site measurements.

more.title: Every 3D Conformal Field Theory Has an L Λ w 1 + ∞ Symmetry
more.abstract: A one-parameter family of deformed L w 1 + ∞ soft symmetry algebras acting on tree-level gravitational theories in AdS 4 has recently been discovered; it is denoted L Λ w 1 + ∞ . Here, we show that all CFT 3 s , including those dual to quantum gravity on AdS 4 , admit an L Λ w 1 + ∞ action generated by the ANEC operator, its conformal descendants, and their commutators. This extends previous tree-level results on these soft symmetries to the strongly coupled quantum regime.

more.title: Bayesian Inference of the Landau Parameter G 0 ′ from Joint Gamow-Teller Measurements
more.abstract: G ′ 0 is the leading-order Landau-Migdal parameter that characterizes the spin-isospin dependent nucleon-nucleon interaction. Consequently, the G ′ 0 is closely related to the Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR), the beta and double-beta decay rates of finite nuclei, the response of hot and dense nucleonic matter that modifies the neutrino-nucleon absorption rates in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) and binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, and finally the critical density for pion condensation in neutron stars. In this letter, for the first time, we report the G ′ 0 with quantified uncertainty in the framework of Bayesian inference, using a self-consistent standard Skyrme Random Phase Approximation (RPA) model and joint constraints from experimental GTR measurements on 208 P b , 132 S n , 90 Z r . Our extracted G 0 ′ at saturation density is 0.48 ± 0.034 , which is close to the prediction of a few existing Skyrme models that consider spin-isospin observables but smaller than the traditional ones extracted from pion-exchange models. The reasons for this deviation, like the value of the nucleon effective mass m * m and the density dependence of G ′ 0 , are investigated. The density-dependent G 0 ′ values extracted in this work may guide the construction of new energy density functionals that aims to self-consistently describe the dense matter properties in the spin-isospin channel.

more.title: Phosphate-Mediated Proton Shuttling Governs Nitrate Electroreduction Selectivity on Copper
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3RR) can be carried out at high reaction rates, yet selectivity to desired ammonia/ammonium remains challenging on catalysts like copper due to a soluble nitrite intermediate. We here find the local microenvironment of NO3RR can influence typical catalyst metrics of rate and selectivity to extents on par with those typically attributed to differences in catalyst formulation. Considering a phosphate-buffered pH 7 medium, we find the high NO3RR rates on Cu exceed the buffering capacity, leading to a surface pH ∼ 13. Accounting for the local proton activity to measure reaction rates at fixed overpotential demonstrates rates approximately an order of magnitude greater compared to a bulk pH 13 electrolyte. In the absence of phosphate, nitrite is kinetically more difficult to reduce on Cu than is nitrate. Inclusion of phosphate─regardless of the bulk pH─leads to the onset of nitrite reduction at comparable potentials to nitrate reduction, and ∼2× higher electron selectivity to ammonia/ammonium compared to without phosphate. Grand canonical density functional theory calculations and microkinetic modeling demonstrate that adsorbed phosphate thermodynamically favors proton abstraction from water under reaction conditions, whereas nitrate and nitrite are incapable of doing so. This effectively leads to a surface-mediated pKa of phosphate species that is different than in solution, which changes the local population of hydrogenated phosphates that can participate in proton-transfer events. This adsorbed phosphate─observed by operando surface-enhanced infrared spectroscopy─stabilizes the nitrite intermediate and promotes proton shuttling from water to nitrite, increasing selectivity to ammonia. more.title: On the Detectability and Measurement of Galactic Bars as a Function of Redshift
more.abstract: The cosmic evolution of galactic bars offers key insights into the dynamical history of disk galaxies. However, studies of high-redshift bars are severely hampered by observational effects such as resolution degradation and surface brightness dimming. To quantify these biases and establish a robust methodology of bar detection and measurement for high-redshift galaxies, we develop an automated pipeline integrating isophotal ellipse fitting and Fourier decomposition. We benchmark its performance using a comprehensive set of mock observations generated by artificially redshifting high-quality images of local barred galaxies to match the background and resolution of Hubble Space Telescope (HST) ( z ≈ 0.5–3) and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) ( z ≈ 1–6) observations. We find that applying standard bar detection criteria derived from local galaxies to high-redshift data results in a severe underestimation of the bar fraction, missing >50% of bars at z > 0.5 in HST imaging and a similar fraction at z > 2 in JWST imaging. Using adaptive, redshift-dependent criteria optimized via mock data achieves recovery rates above 60% out to z ≈ 3 for HST and z ≈ 6 for JWST. The ellipse fitting method significantly outperforms Fourier decomposition in measurement reliability. While ellipse fitting systematically underestimates bar length by ∼4%–36% due to surface brightness dimming, this bias is consistent and correctable ( σ ≈ 0.88–2.22); in contrast, the Fourier method is prone to catastrophic failures ( σ ≈ 2.40–6.14) in the regime of low signal-to-noise ratio. We propose a standardized workflow that prioritizes mock-derived adaptive criteria and ellipse fitting, providing quantitative correction factors and empirical relations that enable future studies to recover intrinsic bar…

more.title: Oblique Kink Waves in Solar Coronal Streamers
more.abstract: Coronal streamer kink waves excited by an impact of coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are routinely used to estimate the coronal Alfvén speed. These estimates generally assume wave propagation parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field directed radially outward to the Sun, in the plane of the sky. However, the geometry of CME impacts naturally allows for oblique propagation. We investigate the properties of obliquely propagating kink waves guided by a plasma slab with a central current sheet representing a coronal streamer stalk. We consider both cold and warm streamer plasmas and analyze the influence of propagation obliquity on wave dispersion, eigenfunctions, and seismological diagnostics. We find that increasing the propagation obliquity reduces the phase speed owing to both projection effects and the intrinsic dependence of the phase speed on the propagation angle. The wave structure also undergoes a gradual transition from a body mode to a surface mode, leading to stronger perturbations at the slab boundaries and enhanced wave localization. Consequently, for a given energy deposited by a CME impact, oblique kink waves are expected to produce larger observable amplitudes than field-aligned waves. Applying the developed theory to streamer waves reported previously, we infer Alfvén speeds in the range of 50–500 km s −1 . We show that neglecting wave propagation obliquity may underestimate the Alfvén speed by up to a factor of 1.5. These results demonstrate that wave propagation obliquity should be taken into account in coronal seismology of streamer waves and that stereoscopic observations will be required to constrain the true propagation direction.

more.title: SiO Maser Line-width Diagnostics of Asymptotic Giant Branch Stars and Red Supergiants: The Red Supergiant-adjacent Region in the FWZI–Luminosity Plane
more.abstract: We investigate whether SiO maser line profiles can distinguish asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars from red supergiants (RSGs) and identify unusual AGB-classified sources near the RSG regime. We compiled 2956 detected SiO maser spectra for 1551 objects and constructed reference samples of 1068 O-rich AGB stars and 36 RSGs. The full width at zero intensity (FWZI) was reliably measured for 1020 AGB stars and 32 RSGs. AGB stars are concentrated at narrow line widths: 81.5% have FWZI < 10 km s −1 , whereas 81.2% of RSGs have FWZI > 15 km s −1 and none have FWZI < 10 km s −1 . Infrared two-color diagrams provide only partial separation. Combining FWZI with luminosities based primarily on quality-filtered Gaia/Bailer-Jones distances, with independent literature distances for several RSGs, reveals a weak tendency for wider SiO maser lines at higher luminosities but no clean boundary. We therefore define an empirical RSG-adjacent region in the FWZI–luminosity plane, 15 ≤ FWZI ≤ 26.6 km s −1 and 3.9 ≤ log ( L / L ⊙ ) ≤ 4.9 , to characterize the high-luminosity, broad-line tail of the AGB-classified sample. Ten sources fall within this region. Using infrared spectral energy distributions, DUSTY fits, OH/H 2 O maser information, and variability, we find that six are most naturally interpreted as luminous AGB-like objects, two warrant follow-up to assess possible high-initial-mass AGB, RSG-like, or super-AGB-related interpretations, and two are less securely constrained because of poor DUSTY fits. The RSG-adjacent region is therefore a physically mixed screening space, not a definitive classification box, for selecting high-priority follow-up targets.

more.title: The Dancing Bonfire: An Unusual Persistent X-Ray Source in M81 Exhibiting Recurrent Luminous Flares
more.abstract: Short-timescale X-ray variability provides a direct probe of unstable accretion onto compact objects, yet extragalactic X-ray binaries (XRBs) with recurrent flaring remain largely unexplored. Here, we present a detailed X-ray study of M81F4 (2CXO J095524.2+690957), a persistently luminous X-ray source toward M81 that exhibits recurrent short X-ray flares. Based on multimission X-ray observations spanning two decades, it is found that M81F4 remains persistently bright at L 0.5−8.0 keV ∼ 10 38 –10 39 erg s −1 , while producing flares lasting a few hundred seconds and reaching peak luminosities of a few 10 39 erg s −1 , with an observed mean (minimum) recurrence time of ∼0.5 day (∼6 ks). The stacked flare profile shows a rapid rise followed by a slower decay, but no significant hardness evolution. Spectral analysis reveals that both the flare and nonflare states are dominated by a hard power-law continuum, with marginal evidence of highly ionized Fe lines in the nonflare state spectrum. These properties disfavor classical Type I and Type II bursts and have no close analog among known XRBs. We favor a magnetized neutron star accreting from an intermediate-mass donor at a persistently high rate, with the flares arising from instabilities at the disk-magnetosphere boundary. If confirmed, M81F4 might represent a hidden population of XRBs in which sustained, magnetically regulated accretion can lead to brief episodes of super-Eddington emission.

more.title: Structural Evolution Accompanies Selectivity Changes during the Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 on a Vicinal Cu(310) Pre-Catalyst
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: The electrocatalytic reduction reaction of CO2 (CO2RR) on copper remains a key strategy for converting greenhouse gases into valuable chemicals, but its large-scale implementation still requires substantial advances in our fundamental understanding of the selectivity-determining properties. Historically, stepped Cu surfaces were thought to have great potential for selective hydrocarbon production during CO2RR. However, it has recently become clear that this distinct facet dependence does not hold for atomically flat Cu(100) and (111) surfaces with large terraces, which primarily yield hydrogen. The present study addresses how the crystallographic orientation and surface history influence CO2RR performance over Cu(310), a vicinal surface with an intrinsically higher density of step-edge defects. Our results show striking analogies to the nonvicinal surfaces, namely, an initially large H2 selectivity but also the formation during operation of mesoscopic imperfections that play a crucial role in the surface activation and catalytic selectivity toward hydrocarbons. More importantly, we report the deactivation mechanism of our vicinal surface upon extended CO2RR operation, which switches from hydrocarbon formation back to hydrogen. Additionally, we demonstrate how the desired hydrocarbon-product selectivity can be regenerated via in situ electrochemical oxidative treatments. Finally, substantial differences in the deactivation kinetics toward H2 evolution vs CO2RR, depending on the oxidative treatment employed, are unveiled. These findings establish a clear link between surface mesoscale morphology, oxidation dynamics, and catalytic function, highlighting the need for controlled surface/chemical state engineering in CO2RR catalysts. These insights offer practical guidance…

more.title: Structural Insights into Erm-Mediated rRNA Methylation Underlying Antibiotic Resistance
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: SAM-dependent Erm enzymes confer resistance to clinically important MLSB antibiotics (macrolides–lincosamides–streptogramin B) by methylation of the rRNA (rRNA) target. However, the molecular basis of the Erm–rRNA interaction remains poorly understood, hindering the development of effective Erm inhibitors to preserve antibiotic efficacy. Here, we integrate NMR and computational data to investigate the interaction between ErmB, prevalent in pathogenic Gram-positive bacteria, and a minimal RNA substrate mimicking the rRNA target. We demonstrate that Erm–RNA complex formation is critically dependent on the SAM cofactor, which shapes the conformational space of the entire catalytic domain, priming ErmB for specific recognition of its RNA substrate. Using NMR-guided docking, we derive experimentally validated structural models of the ErmB–RNA complex that reveal a vast and dynamic binding interface comprising ErmB’s N- and C-terminal domains, as well as the cationic interdomain cleft. These insights into the Erm enzyme function provide a foundation for the rational design of potent and selective drugs to combat pathogenic bacteria.

more.title: What if we were to design transport in aqueous electrolytes using learnings from lithium battery research?
more.abstract: Electrolyte design has played a crucial role in the development of lithium batteries for a range of applications. Of late, there is a renewed interest in developing a new generation of aqueous batteries to cheaply store energy for the grid. Given the amount of research our community has carried out developing lithium electrolytes, an intriguing possibility is to leverage these learnings to accelerate the development of aqueous electrolytes - especially when battery development requires decades of effort. We herein examine this argument to guide aqueous battery electrolyte research. We discuss the current understanding of transport mechanisms across molecular and continuum scales that can be readily applied to advance aqueous electrolytes. Based on such multiscale understanding, we propose the concept of transport maps to quantitatively assess electrolyte advances. We additionally synthesize the aqueous electrolyte transport property measurement literature to propose bottom-up design heuristics. The discussion is intentionally confined to binary electrolytes made up of a salt dissolved in water to uncover the nature of ion-ion and ion-water interactions that can be combined to imagine new aqueous electrolytes of varying complexities.

more.title: Data-Driven Electrolyte Design by Electrotopological State Descriptors for Na-Ion Batteries with Minimal Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Dissolution
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) determines the cycling reversibility of Na-ion batteries (NIBs). However, the high solubility of the Na-SEI continuously depletes the limited Na inventory in full cells, leading to accelerated electrolyte consumption and rapid capacity loss. To date, no general electrolyte design principles have been established to mitigate SEI dissolution, plaguing high Na-ion reversibility as an unsolved challenge. Herein, we quantitatively evaluate SEI dissolution across a broad range of NIB electrolytes and employ a closed-loop data-driven approach to correlate the dissolution behavior with over 200 electrolyte physicochemical descriptors. Among them, the solvent average electrotopological state (EState) index shows the strongest correlation with the SEI solubility. Guided by this insight, we designed high-EState electrolytes that suppressed SEI dissolution to only 6% of that in conventional electrolytes. The resulting minimal Na loss enabled a near-unity average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% over 1000 cycles in a hard carbon||NaMn0.33Fe0.33Ni0.33O2 full cell with all earth-abundant materials, successfully extending the End-of-Life battery model to Na-ion chemistry. This work elucidates quantitative correlations between electrolyte physicochemical properties and SEI dissolution, proposes EState-based electrolyte design principles with enhanced electrode–electrolyte interphase stability, and provides fundamental guidance to interphase designs for sustainable NIBs with high reversibility.

more.title: Porous materials for sulfur dioxide capture from flue gas
more.abstract: This review summarizes recent advances in porous materials for SO 2 capture, compares their adsorption mechanisms and structure–performance relationships, and highlights challenges and prospects for flue gas desulfurization.

more.title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO 2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
more.abstract: Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO 2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady‐state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO 2 hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO 2 hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO 2 hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO 2 activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo‐ and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

more.title: Single-Atom Catalysts for Biomass Valorization
more.abstract: Biomass, the only renewable organic carbon resource on Earth, offers a promising feedstock for producing value-added chemicals and fuels. However, the principal challenge in biomass valorization stems from the inherent complexity of its functional groups, necessitating catalysts capable of precisely activating specific C–O/C═O/C═C bonds while suppressing undesired side reactions. Single-atom catalysts (SACs), featuring unique geometric and electronic structures as well as high atomic utilization efficiency, have shown potential for highly effective biomass conversion in thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. Drawing upon recent continuous efforts on SACs in biomass valorization, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances in applying SACs to the transformation of main components of lignocellulosic biomass and their platform molecules. Structure–activity relationships and catalytic behavior of SACs under different external stimuli (e.g., thermal, electrical, and photonic) are emphasized, showcasing their innovative applications. The important factors governing catalytic activity and selectivity with a particular focus on the geometric and electronic structures of active sites are discussed, aiming to derive fundamental principles for the rational design of efficient and selective catalysts for biomass valorization. Finally, an outlook highlights the key challenges and prospects in this flourishing field.

more.title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment
more.abstract: (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

more.title: Language model teams as distributed systems
more.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
more.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are growing increasingly powerful. Yet, fundamental constraints on the reasoning, memory, and performance of individual models has sparked recent interest in scaling abilities using LLM teams. With growing deployment of LLM teams at scale, there is a need for principled guidelines for when teams help, how many agents to use, and how structure impacts performance. Rather than building these teams through trial-and-error, we propose using distributed systems as a formal foundation for designing and evaluating LLM teams. Under this formal framework, we derive predictions about how task structure and team architecture should shape performance. Empirical evidence supports these predictions: LLM team scaling follows classical distributed computing laws based on the structure of a task, and centralized and decentralized architectures exhibit the asymmetric vulnerabilities predicted by distributed systems theory. These results establish distributed computing as a generative framework that yields testable, quantitative predictions about LLM team behavior and informs the construction of more efficient and capable teams.

more.title: Symmetry-Guided Prediction of Magnetic-Ordered Ground States
more.abstract: Given the scarcity of experimentally confirmed magnetic structures, the reliable prediction of magnetic ground states is crucial yet remains a long-sought challenge due to the complex magnetic potential energy landscape. Here, we propose a symmetry-guided framework that systematically generates realistic magnetic configurations without requiring any experimental input or prior assumptions such as propagation vectors. The framework incorporates the recently developed oriented spin space group formalism, which captures symmetry-breaking pathways induced by both magnetic ordering and spin-orbit coupling. By performing nonrelativistic and relativistic first-principles calculations, we further establish the energy ladder of the generated magnetic configurations. Exemplified by three prominent unconventional magnets MnTe, Mn 3 Sn , and CoNb 3 S 6 , we demonstrate that only a few dozen first-principles calculations are sufficient to identify the ground-state magnetic structure. To demonstrate the universality and robustness of our approach, we conduct large-scale benchmark tests on the MAGNDATA database. Our framework successfully reproduces experimentally reported magnetic structures for 73% of the surveyed materials. Furthermore, in a high-throughput first-principles benchmark involving 305 compounds, 82% of experimentally reported magnetic geometries are accurately captured within an energy tolerance of 5 meV per magnetic atom from the computed ground state. Beyond reproducing known magnetic configurations, our framework further predicts a variety of low-energy metastable phases, including altermagnets, spin-orbit magnets, and noncollinear antiferromagnets with spin splitting or geometric Hall effect. Our approach is implemented as the open online program SPINGEN,…

more.title: Universal spectral correlations in open Floquet systems with localized leaks
more.abstract: We investigate how non-Hermitian random-matrix universality emerges in a physical Floquet system with localized leakage. As a concrete example, we consider the leaky quantum standard map (L-QSM) of the kicked rotor. Since the closed map exhibits circular orthogonal ensemble (COE) statistics, we compare its spectral properties with those of the truncated circular orthogonal ensemble (TCOE), which models localized leakage by removing columns from a COE matrix and thus provides the natural finite-dimensional random-matrix benchmark for the open system. The local spectral correlations of the L-QSM and TCOE show excellent agreement, exhibiting a crossover from the COE limit, recovered only when the truncation is smaller than one full column, to the universal statistics of the non-Hermitian symmetry class A I † , reached when the number of truncated columns is n L ≳ 100 , essentially independently of the matrix sizes N studied. This shows that the crossover is controlled by the number of truncated columns, n L , rather than by the physical size of the leak, Δ q = n L / N . In contrast, the global spectral properties follow a different crossover. At intermediate leakage, the L-QSM and TCOE retain an accumulation of long-lived resonances near the unit circle and remain far from the Ginibre circular law. The L-QSM additionally exhibits system-specific features, with an excess of very short-lived resonances and phase-space stickiness affecting long-lived resonances. Only at strong leakage does the TCOE density of states approach the circular law, suggesting the same limiting behavior for the L-QSM. Our results show that local bulk correlations reach non-Hermitian universality at weaker leakage than global spectral properties, which retain system-specific features over a broader…

more.title: Rules-and-facts model for simultaneous generalization and memorization in neural networks
more.abstract: A key capability of modern neural networks is their capacity to simultaneously learn underlying rules and memorize specific facts or exceptions. Yet, theoretical understanding of this dual capability remains limited. We introduce the Rules-and-Facts (RAF) model, a minimal solvable setting that enables precise characterization of this phenomenon by bridging two classical lines of work in the statistical physics of learning: the teacher-student framework for generalization and Gardner-style capacity analysis for memorization. In the RAF model, a fraction 1 − ε of training labels is generated by a structured teacher rule, while a fraction ε consists of unstructured facts with random labels. We characterize when the learner can simultaneously recover the underlying rule - allowing generalization to new data - and memorize the unstructured examples. Our results quantify how overparameterization enables the simultaneous realization of these two objectives: sufficient excess capacity supports memorization, while regularization and the choice of kernel or nonlinearity control the allocation of capacity between rule learning and memorization. Experiments on a CIFAR10-based RAF task show that the qualitative trade-off persists for fixed kernels, whereas representations learned by deeper neural networks substantially mitigate it, preserving factual recall while improving generalization. The RAF model provides a theoretical foundation for understanding how modern neural networks can infer structure while storing rare or non-compressible information.

more.title: Taxing Homeowners Who Can't or Won't Borrow
more.abstract: Using high-frequency administrative data covering millions of US homeowners, I document three novel facts about homeowner responses to property tax increases driven by rising home values. First, non-migrating homeowners cut consumption, exhibit financial distress, and do not borrow against their higher home values. Second, heterogeneity analysis shows that consumption responses do not vary by liquidity, consistent with savings target behavior. In contrast, distress responses are concentrated among liquidity-constrained homeowners. Many homeowners report being debt averse and therefore unwilling to borrow in order to avoid illiquidity and distress. Third, tax hikes induce migration—partly by displacing illiquid homeowners—but do not accelerate neighborhood change. A simple welfare framework reveals that the largest costs of property taxes arise from financial distress, suggesting welfare gains from policies that limit taxes for liquidity-constrained households.

more.title: Diagnosing the Effects of Spectroscopic Training Set Imperfection on Photometric Redshift Performance
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Most LSST extragalactic science will rely on photometric redshifts (photo-z) to extract distance information for the galaxies. However, an incomplete or non-representative training set can introduce bias into photo-z estimation. It is necessary to understand how various forms of training set imperfection, such as incompleteness and non-trivial spectroscopic target selection, affect photo-z estimation algorithms, and to identify metrics best-suited to quantify the impact. This work aims to systematically study metrics for diagnosing how various photo-z methods react to certain types of training set incompleteness and non-representativeness. We use methods available through the open-source Python library Redshift Assessment Infrastructure Layers (RAIL) to systematically test the algorithms CMNN, GPz, FlexZBoost, and PZFlow on mock training data degraded in accordance with several existing spectroscopic sky surveys, as well as under conditions of inverse redshift incompleteness, which approximately mimics observed patterns of incompleteness at high redshift. We employ the algorithm TrainZ as a control. Finally, we quantify photo-z algorithm performance using a variety of statistical metrics implemented externally to RAIL. We determine that the Kullback-Liebler Divergence, Wasserstein Distance, and Probability Integral Transform are particularly informative metrics with which to assess the impact of training set imperfection on algorithmic performance. We also find that inverse redshift incompleteness effects alone lack the complexity to realistically represent anticipated training data.

more.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
more.abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. To examine the present scheme, we analyze the MAGNDATA database and find that 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. When the k index is fixed to its experimental value, the number of magnetic structures generated is on average about nine, also demonstrating the high efficiency of this scheme. Next, to quantitatively assess computational and predictive performance, we perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. more.title: Limits of Disclosure in Search Markets
more.abstract: This paper examines competitive information disclosure in search markets with a mix of selective consumers, who search costlessly, and casual consumers, who incur positive search costs. Selective consumers incentivize truthful disclosure; casual consumers, concealment. With both types, the equilibrium features partial disclosure, which persists despite intense competition. Casual consumers may search actively, but only in small markets. While selective consumers benefit from increased competition, casual consumers may be harmed. Changes in search costs have non-monotone effects: the equilibrium approaches full disclosure as the cost approaches zero or the mean valuation. When costs are high, further increases raise equilibrium informativeness and the welfare of selective consumers, while reducing the welfare of casual consumers.

more.title: Gut-bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells contribute to HIV persistence during ART
more.abstract: Antigen specificities of most HIV reservoir cells remain poorly defined. We examined whether CD4 + T cells specific for gut bacterial antigens contribute to HIV replication and persistence. Gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells were markedly reduced in viremic people living with HIV (PWH) and remained incompletely restored despite antiretroviral therapy (ART), with those expressing markers of HIV permissiveness being preferentially depleted. Circulating gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells from PWH on ART displayed lower TCR β diversity and persistent functional disruption, characterized by attenuation of canonical effector programs and a higher proportion of cells with cytotoxic features. By contrast, rectum-localized bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells from the same individuals exhibited a tolerogenic profile, highlighting the compartment-specific function of these cells. Near-full-length proviral sequencing revealed clonal expansions of HIV genomes within circulating gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells from ART-treated participants, with evidence of cross-reactivity across multiple bacterial species. Genetically intact proviruses were enriched in Salmonella Typhimurium-specific CD4 + T cells. These findings suggest that gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells are preferentially targeted during untreated HIV infection and incompletely restored by ART, harboring genetically intact HIV genomes and constituting an antigen-driven reservoir in which chronic stimulation by gut microbial antigens promotes clonal proliferation and long-term HIV persistence during ART.

more.title: Revisiting the enigmatic sixth star cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: The Fornax dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy is one of only two Local Group dSphs that host a population of globular star clusters (GCs), the present-day properties of which have often been used to investigate the nature of the dark matter. An additional overdensity of stars called Fornax 6, lying at a projected distance of ~0.3 kpc from the galaxy centre, was recently identified as a sixth GC residing in Fornax. However, this conclusion was based on relatively shallow photometric observations and a limited number of spectra. Here, we reinvestigate the nature of Fornax 6 by analysing MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations alongside deep GMOS-S imagery. Using a sample of 131 spectra of red giant and red clump stars, we confirm the Fornax 6 overdensity as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with respect to the surrounding field population. Specifically, we identify 43 likely members associated with the cluster, from which we measure [Fe/H] = −0.63 ± 0.03 dex, vₗₒₛ = 50.8^(+0.8)_(-0.7) km s⁻¹, and σ ᵥ = 3.3^(+1.4)_(-1.9) km s⁻¹. The main-sequence turn-off, observed here for the first time, strongly suggests that these stars are coeval and well described by a ~3 Gyr old isochrone. The cluster is characterised by an irregular morphology, a large half-light radius (Rₕ=8.8^(+1.1)_(-1.3)pc), a small flattening (e < 0.26, 68% upper limit), and low luminosity (MV = −5.0 ± 0.4). Our improved characterisation of Fornax 6 supports its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax’s unique GC system.

more.title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
more.abstract: Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl interface increases the discharge current at which voiding commences tenfold, from 0.2 to 2 mA cm −2 at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm −2 at 30 °C and 8 mA cm −2 at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

more.title: MIDIS: Strong H β +[O iii ] Line Emitters at z ≳ 9
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We search for strong Hβ+[O iii] line emitters at z = 9.4 − 11.3 in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field using ultra-deep MIRI/F560W imaging from the MIRI Deep Imaging Survey. Three galaxies show F560W flux excesses relative to their continuum, consistent with Hβ+[O iii] emission. We derive rest-frame Hβ+[O iii] equivalent widths of EW^(Hβ+[OIII])ᵣₑₛₜ ≃ 700-1500Å, placing them among the most extreme nebular line emitters at this epoch. Combining our sources with 15 spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at z > 9 with published Hβ+[O iii] measurements, we derive a median EW^(Hβ+[Oiii])ᵣₑₛₜ = 1433Å with median absolute deviation of 670 Å. We find no evidence for an increase or decline in EW^(Hβ+[O_III])ᵣₑₛₜ at z > 9. Binning the combined z > 9 sample by UV luminosity, we find higher equivalent widths in more UV-luminous systems. While consistent with trends at z = 6 − 9, the difference is not significant, and subject to heterogeneous sample selection. No significant anti-correlation between Hβ+[O iii] equivalent width and stellar mass is found, although a fit suggests a trend consistent with lower-redshift observations. We place a first constraint on the Hβ+[O iii] line luminosity function at z ≃ 9 − 11 (Φ ∼ 10−3.3 Mpc−3 dex−1 at log (L_(Hβ+[Oᵢii])/ erg s⁻¹) = 42.45) consistent with a decline relative to z ≃ 7 − 8. We derive ionising photon production efficiencies of log (ξion/Hz erg−1) = 25.3 − 25.5, and find tentative trends between ξion and EW^(Hβ+[O_III])ᵣₑₛₜ, and between ξion and β, consistent with those observed at z = 6 − 9. These results suggest that the physical conditions governing nebular emission and its link to the UV continuum are in place at z > 9.

more.title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
From Design to Disclosure
more.abstract: We study the role of hard information in contractual and market settings in which the receiver can flexibly adjust allocations and transfers in response to the sender's disclosure. These settings include monopoly pricing, insurance contracting, and policy negotiations. Across these settings, the sender is worst off if she reveals her type completely because the receiver would then adjust the terms of trade to extract her surplus. Taking this feature as our central departure from the literature, we characterize the entire set of equilibrium payoffs in these disclosure games. We prove an equivalence result: a payoff profile can be approximated by an equilibrium of the disclosure game if and only if it can be achieved through information design. Thus, there exist equilibria in which the sender obtains approximately her commitment payoff.

more.title: Optimal Incentive Design for Decentralized Dynamic Matching Markets
more.abstract: In decentralized dynamic matching markets, agents can benefit from sharing resources, but they will collaborate only if properly incentivized. Motivated by applications such as multihospital kidney exchanges and job-hunting markets, this paper proposes novel monetary and nonmonetary mechanisms to incentivize collaboration in such decentralized dynamic markets. We study a model in which multiple self-interested agents manage local multiway dynamic matching problems. Jobs of different types arrive stochastically at each agent, expire after a limited time, and yield rewards when matched. An agent’s job backlog and actions are the agent’s private information, and each agent aims to maximize its long-run average matching reward. We design simple mechanisms that incentivize agents to submit all jobs upon arrival, thereby enabling centralized matching. Our first mechanism, the marginal-value (MV) mechanism, reimburses agents based on the MV of their submitted jobs. This can be implemented in a nonmonetary way by randomly selecting an agent (with a specified probability) to perform a match and collect the associated matching reward. We show that under the MV mechanism, full job submission constitutes an approximate Nash equilibrium—that is, the gain from unilateral deviation vanishes as the number of agents grows. To further eliminate incentives for deviation, we propose a refined mechanism, the MV-plus-credit (MVC) mechanism, and show that, when the number of agents exceeds a constant threshold, full job submission constitutes a stronger oblivious equilibrium. Numerical experiments based on kidney exchange data demonstrate that the gains from deviation under our mechanisms are small even in moderately sized markets. more.title: One year of broadband radio monitoring of the enigmatic transient GRB 250702B reveals the evolution of the relativistic jet
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We present an extensive radio monitoring campaign of the unique extragalactic transient GRB 250702B, associated with unprecedentedly long duration gamma-ray emission, lasting over 3 hr. Our observations span 0.65–233 GHz from 6–356 d (observer frame) post-discovery. The radio emission shows a smoothly evolving peaked synchrotron spectrum consistent with an adiabatic shock expanding into a stratified ambient medium (ne∝R−k; k = 1.5 − 2). We detect significant variability in the low frequency (≤3 GHz) light curves which we interpret as interstellar scintillation, placing an approximate bound on the blast wave image size of 1.2 × 1016 ≲ R⊥ ≲ 5 × 1017 cm. The temporal evolution of the flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies suggest the shock that powers the radio emission is potentially a wide-angle θj ≳ 15 deg, low Lorentz factor (Γ ≲ 10) jet, or a narrow θj ≲ 2 deg (Γ0 > 50) highly relativistic jet. A narrow jet is expected for a stellar-mass black hole engine, such as a helium star merger, and the beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is consistent with the known distribution for long GRBs (EK ~ 1051 erg). The wide-angle jet scenario would instead require a progenitor involving prolonged accretion. We derive and show an intermediate or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event are viable possibilities. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is on the low end of the known distribution for relativistic SMBH TDEs (EK ~ 1050 erg). We disfavour an SMBH TDE due to lack of compatibility with the observed timescales. The detection of a jet shut off within the next year would favour a WD-IMBH TDE due to the shorter theoretical duration of super-Eddington accretion than the main-sequence TDE channels.

The horizontal dashed purple line shows the 3 σ 1.28 GHz upper limit on the host galaxy emission from a MeerKAT observation 2000 d (observer frame) prior to the transient occurring. shortlist.title: Dark matter constraints from small-scale cosmic structure
shortlist.abstract: Small-scale cosmic structure provides a powerful test of the fundamental nature of dark matter. A wide range of dark matter models impact matter clustering on small scales, including warm, fuzzy, and (self-)interacting dark matter. In these scenarios, dark matter physics such as free-streaming, wave interference, and self/Standard Model interactions alter the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos. Cosmological and astrophysical probes of small-scale structure—including dwarf galaxies, strong lensing, the Lyman- α forest, stellar streams, and high-redshift galaxies—are therefore sensitive to these effects. Here, we review dark matter constraints provided by small-scale structure, focusing on observables that probe scales smaller than ∼ 1 M p c , which define the frontier of current measurements. We summarize how these constraints have been translated to limits on microphysical dark matter models, and we discuss key modeling uncertainties and observational systematics. Finally, we highlight the growing importance of probe combination and simulation-based inference for this field, and we overview upcoming observational facilities that will sharpen small-scale structure tests of dark matter physics.

shortlist.title: Field-level Inference from Galaxies: Baryon Acoustic Oscillation Reconstruction
shortlist.abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) underpin the key cosmological results from modern spectroscopic galaxy surveys, but nonlinear gravitational evolution limits the precision achievable with traditional analysis methods. To overcome this, we develop field-level inference for BAO, first reconstructing the initial linear density field and then fitting the BAO signal therein. We benchmark three reconstruction methods: (i) traditional reconstruction based on linear theory, (ii) explicit field-level inference using differentiable forward modeling with hybrid effective field theory, and (iii) implicit field-level inference using a convolutional neural network to augment traditional reconstruction. Using DESI-like luminous red galaxy (LRG) and Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS) catalogs, we find that field-level approaches significantly sharpen the BAO feature relative to traditional reconstruction. For LRGs, explicit field-level inference improves constraints on the BAO scale parameters ( α iso , α ap ) by 23%–26%, while implicit inference improves constraints by 33%–34%, corresponding to a 2.2× improvement in figure of merit (FoM). For the higher-density, lower-redshift BGS sample, field-level inference enables information extraction from smaller scales, yielding an improvement in constraints of up to 46%, corresponding to a 3.2× improvement in FoM. Crucially, we address longstanding concerns regarding the robustness of field-level reconstruction by leveraging 1000 mock realizations to perform extensive coverage tests. Our results are both unbiased and statistically well calibrated, maintaining nominal coverage even when using tight simulation-informed priors and under model misspecification.

shortlist.title: Direct wave is not a meaningful test of horizon properties
shortlist.abstract: Recently, a distinct component of black hole binary merger radiation, named the direct wave, has been identified. The frequency and damping time of the direct wave have been associated with properties of the remnant horizon. This has led to direct wave based analysis of GW250114, including a test of Hawking’s area law. However, as we demonstrate here for comparable mass binaries using numerical relativity strain data, the direct wave frequency is not correlated with the horizon frequency or surface gravity, other than an incidental crossing around χ f ≈ 0.7 corresponding closely to the remnant spin of GW250114. Because the damping time shows significant evolution a single damped sinusoid model with a fixed damping time is not appropriate to model the entire direct wave, except for short time intervals. We further show that an evolving frequency model based on horizon properties also does not model the direct wave component for systems with large remnant spins. We demonstrate that testing Hawking’s area law with a horizon frequency based on the direct wave interpretation may lead to apparent violations of Hawking’s area law when no violation actually occurs. Our results therefore indicate that the direct wave is not a reliable probe of the remnant horizon’s properties for comparable mass mergers.

shortlist.title: Diffusive Dynamics of Nonstabilizerness
shortlist.abstract: Symmetries shape the quantum-information dynamics of many-body systems, but their effect on nonstabilizerness, the resource complementary to entanglement, is less understood. We compute the stabilizer Renyi entropy, a measure of nonstabilizerness, in U(1)-symmetric one-dimensional random circuits. The disorder-averaged dynamics is captured by a four-replica tensor network, which we evaluate by S4-adapted infinite time-evolving block decimation (iTEBD) directly in the thermodynamic limit. Together with a hydrodynamic argument, our results identify a diffusive universality class for the late-time approach of nonstabilizerness to its random-state value, with the stabilizer Renyi entropy gap closing as 1/t. The same scaling is verified in an energy-conserving nonintegrable Ising chain. More broadly, our framework provides a hydrodynamic perspective on nonstabilizerness generation and offers insight into the design of approximate Haar-random states in Hamiltonian dynamics.

shortlist.title: Assembling extensive quantum Fisher information in stabilizer systems
shortlist.abstract: We introduce a systematic framework to construct nonlocal observables with extensive quantum Fisher information (QFI) density in stabilizer codes. The construction maps stabilizer generators to dual Ising spins whose correlators equal string order parameters, converting hidden nonlocal order into a possibly metrologically accessible observable. Applying this to monitored cluster codes and the toric code, we identify transitions in the QFI scaling from an extensive regime—where long-range string order prevails—to an intensive one driven by competing single-site measurements.

shortlist.title: Every 3D Conformal Field Theory Has an L Λ w 1 + ∞ Symmetry
shortlist.abstract: A one-parameter family of deformed L w 1 + ∞ soft symmetry algebras acting on tree-level gravitational theories in AdS 4 has recently been discovered; it is denoted L Λ w 1 + ∞ . Here, we show that all CFT 3 s , including those dual to quantum gravity on AdS 4 , admit an L Λ w 1 + ∞ action generated by the ANEC operator, its conformal descendants, and their commutators. This extends previous tree-level results on these soft symmetries to the strongly coupled quantum regime.

shortlist.title: Highly Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Achieving high crystallinity in three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly beyond 4-connected tetrahedral nodes toward higher-connectivity building units. Here, we report the rapid synthesis of three highly crystalline triptycene-based COFs (COF-563, −564, and −565) as well-faceted, micrometer-sized crystals under mild conditions within 24 h. By employing rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic triptycene-based building units, hexakis(4-aminophenyl/4-formylphenyl)triptycene (Trip-NH2/Trip-CHO), we access a topological regime of three-dimensional (3D) COFs that includes the established hea and stp nets as well as an unprecedented (6,6)-connected htp topology. These frameworks are constructed through reticulation of the triptycene nodes with tetrahedral (tetra(4-anilyl)methane (TAM)), rectangular (pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetraaniline (PyTTA)), and hexagonal (hexakis(4′-formyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)benzene (HFBB)) complementary linkers to yield the hea, stp, and htp structures, respectively. The resulting materials exhibit permanent porosity with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface areas of up to 3769 m2 g–1─approaching a 2-fold increase over previously reported values for related topologies─and thermal stability up to 500 °C. This work establishes a versatile platform for the rapid formation of highly crystalline 3D organic frameworks and provides a blueprint for designing complex, highly porous architectures with controlled topology.

shortlist.title: Turnovers Drive Supported Metal Nanoparticle Catalyst Surface Reconstruction to Kinetically Trapped Metastable Structures
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Supported metal catalysts often operate with high adsorbate coverages that can alter nanoparticle structures as compared to the clean catalyst. Such restructuring is typically described within an equilibrium picture that assumes that nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages adopt their thermodynamically preferred state. Here, we challenge this assumption and propose that under conditions of high adsorbate coverage and fast turnovers of surface species, supported metal nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages can become kinetically trapped in metastable states. We studied CO adsorption–desorption quasi-equilibrium on Pt/γ-Al2O3 using in situ IR spectroscopy and chemisorption as a function of temperature (300–650 K), CO pressure (10–2–10–4 bar), and visible photon flux (0–2 W cm–2 440 nm photons). The adsorbed CO IR band area increases with temperature and photon flux, contrary to equilibrium predictions of decreasing coverage. Estimates of apparent Pt dispersion and CO desorption rates, along with the reversibility of IR spectral changes, support the hypothesis that when CO turnovers are faster than Pt atomic rearrangements to their equilibrium state, the catalyst is driven into metastable states. We estimate atomic rearrangements time scales of 10–1–10–3 s on CO-covered Pt nanoparticles at ∼500–600 K. Grand-canonical sampling calculations show that equilibrium Pt–CO structures cannot reproduce the experimental IR trends, implying the presence of off-equilibrium coverages, structures, or both. By matching the experimental trend, theory identifies a plausible flat, nonequilibrium free-energy region that can facilitate kinetic trapping of metastable catalyst states. These results highlight the need for theoretical and experimental approaches targeting…

shortlist.title: Phosphate-Mediated Proton Shuttling Governs Nitrate Electroreduction Selectivity on Copper
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3RR) can be carried out at high reaction rates, yet selectivity to desired ammonia/ammonium remains challenging on catalysts like copper due to a soluble nitrite intermediate. We here find the local microenvironment of NO3RR can influence typical catalyst metrics of rate and selectivity to extents on par with those typically attributed to differences in catalyst formulation. Considering a phosphate-buffered pH 7 medium, we find the high NO3RR rates on Cu exceed the buffering capacity, leading to a surface pH ∼ 13. Accounting for the local proton activity to measure reaction rates at fixed overpotential demonstrates rates approximately an order of magnitude greater compared to a bulk pH 13 electrolyte. In the absence of phosphate, nitrite is kinetically more difficult to reduce on Cu than is nitrate. Inclusion of phosphate─regardless of the bulk pH─leads to the onset of nitrite reduction at comparable potentials to nitrate reduction, and ∼2× higher electron selectivity to ammonia/ammonium compared to without phosphate. Grand canonical density functional theory calculations and microkinetic modeling demonstrate that adsorbed phosphate thermodynamically favors proton abstraction from water under reaction conditions, whereas nitrate and nitrite are incapable of doing so. This effectively leads to a surface-mediated pKa of phosphate species that is different than in solution, which changes the local population of hydrogenated phosphates that can participate in proton-transfer events. This adsorbed phosphate─observed by operando surface-enhanced infrared spectroscopy─stabilizes the nitrite intermediate and promotes proton shuttling from water to nitrite, increasing selectivity to ammonia. The presence of a pH gradient further…

shortlist.title: The Milky Way Joins the Extragalactic World. I. PHANGS
shortlist.abstract: Complete catalogs of molecular clouds in the Milky Way allow analysis of the molecular medium and the star formation properties of the Milky Way that closely follows the method used for nearby galaxies, in particular in the PHANGS project. The dependencies of the depletion time on other properties of molecular gas in the Milky Way are similar to those of other galaxies when analyzed in an analogous way. They exhibit a large scatter and relatively weak correlations. The strongest correlation is a decrease in depletion time with increasing velocity dispersion. We explore the effects of spatial resolution, sensitivity, cloud identificaton method, averaging method, and tracer choice on our results. Metallicity effects in converting observations to mass can have a substantial impact. Somewhat fortuitously, differences in conversion methods between PHANGS and the Milky Way do not affect the current comparison. Inadequate spatial resolution, resulting in unresolved cloud structure, has the most important effect on the interpretation of both extragalactic observations and existing catalogs of Milky Way clouds.

shortlist.title: On the Detectability and Measurement of Galactic Bars as a Function of Redshift
shortlist.abstract: The cosmic evolution of galactic bars offers key insights into the dynamical history of disk galaxies. However, studies of high-redshift bars are severely hampered by observational effects such as resolution degradation and surface brightness dimming. To quantify these biases and establish a robust methodology of bar detection and measurement for high-redshift galaxies, we develop an automated pipeline integrating isophotal ellipse fitting and Fourier decomposition. We benchmark its performance using a comprehensive set of mock observations generated by artificially redshifting high-quality images of local barred galaxies to match the background and resolution of Hubble Space Telescope (HST) ( z ≈ 0.5–3) and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) ( z ≈ 1–6) observations. We find that applying standard bar detection criteria derived from local galaxies to high-redshift data results in a severe underestimation of the bar fraction, missing >50% of bars at z > 0.5 in HST imaging and a similar fraction at z > 2 in JWST imaging. Using adaptive, redshift-dependent criteria optimized via mock data achieves recovery rates above 60% out to z ≈ 3 for HST and z ≈ 6 for JWST. The ellipse fitting method significantly outperforms Fourier decomposition in measurement reliability. While ellipse fitting systematically underestimates bar length by ∼4%–36% due to surface brightness dimming, this bias is consistent and correctable ( σ ≈ 0.88–2.22); in contrast, the Fourier method is prone to catastrophic failures ( σ ≈ 2.40–6.14) in the regime of low signal-to-noise ratio. We propose a standardized workflow that prioritizes mock-derived adaptive criteria and ellipse fitting, providing quantitative correction factors and empirical relations that enable future studies to recover intrinsic bar…
