shortlist.title: Cycles of discourse, speech dysfluency, and active inference.
shortlist.abstract: Speech is a complex motor and social act. We must not only produce and understand sequences of variable-length words formed from ordered syllables but also speak and listen in turn. This theoretical article introduces a computational model of speech production and auditory segmentation based on sequences of discrete phonemes . The purpose of this model is to develop a vehicle for testing (in silico) hypotheses about the mechanisms that govern the loss of speech fluency , something may occur transiently in people who stutter or progressively in various neurodegenerative conditions. The modeling presented here employs Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes that provide a useful generic formulation for specifying the internal model that our brains might use to describe dynamic environments in which they can exert partial control and make partial observations. The core features of the specific model used here are as follows: (a) a reciprocal mapping from words to sequences of varying numbers of phonemes and (b) a common subset of states for both speech generation and speech perception . A further novel feature is a social component in which one must infer who is speaking (oneself or another person). We propose a series of hypotheses about the computational mechanisms that might underwrite speech breakdown. For example, we demonstrate that reducing the precision in the next word introduces pauses and start-of-word repetitions of the sort associated with stuttering . We examine the patterns of behavior and belief-updating predicted by each of these hypotheses, with implications for both speaking and listening . Finally, we discuss plausible neural substrates for the underlying message passing that might be amenable to interrogation with functional imaging.

shortlist.title: Oblique Kink Waves in Solar Coronal Streamers
shortlist.abstract: Coronal streamer kink waves excited by an impact of coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are routinely used to estimate the coronal Alfvén speed. These estimates generally assume wave propagation parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field directed radially outward to the Sun, in the plane of the sky. However, the geometry of CME impacts naturally allows for oblique propagation. We investigate the properties of obliquely propagating kink waves guided by a plasma slab with a central current sheet representing a coronal streamer stalk. We consider both cold and warm streamer plasmas and analyze the influence of propagation obliquity on wave dispersion, eigenfunctions, and seismological diagnostics. We find that increasing the propagation obliquity reduces the phase speed owing to both projection effects and the intrinsic dependence of the phase speed on the propagation angle. The wave structure also undergoes a gradual transition from a body mode to a surface mode, leading to stronger perturbations at the slab boundaries and enhanced wave localization. Consequently, for a given energy deposited by a CME impact, oblique kink waves are expected to produce larger observable amplitudes than field-aligned waves. Applying the developed theory to streamer waves reported previously, we infer Alfvén speeds in the range of 50–500 km s −1 . We show that neglecting wave propagation obliquity may underestimate the Alfvén speed by up to a factor of 1.5. These results demonstrate that wave propagation obliquity should be taken into account in coronal seismology of streamer waves and that stereoscopic observations will be required to constrain the true propagation direction.

shortlist.title: Structural Evolution Accompanies Selectivity Changes during the Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 on a Vicinal Cu(310) Pre-Catalyst
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: The electrocatalytic reduction reaction of CO2 (CO2RR) on copper remains a key strategy for converting greenhouse gases into valuable chemicals, but its large-scale implementation still requires substantial advances in our fundamental understanding of the selectivity-determining properties. Historically, stepped Cu surfaces were thought to have great potential for selective hydrocarbon production during CO2RR. However, it has recently become clear that this distinct facet dependence does not hold for atomically flat Cu(100) and (111) surfaces with large terraces, which primarily yield hydrogen. The present study addresses how the crystallographic orientation and surface history influence CO2RR performance over Cu(310), a vicinal surface with an intrinsically higher density of step-edge defects. Our results show striking analogies to the nonvicinal surfaces, namely, an initially large H2 selectivity but also the formation during operation of mesoscopic imperfections that play a crucial role in the surface activation and catalytic selectivity toward hydrocarbons. More importantly, we report the deactivation mechanism of our vicinal surface upon extended CO2RR operation, which switches from hydrocarbon formation back to hydrogen. Additionally, we demonstrate how the desired hydrocarbon-product selectivity can be regenerated via in situ electrochemical oxidative treatments. Finally, substantial differences in the deactivation kinetics toward H2 evolution vs CO2RR, depending on the oxidative treatment employed, are unveiled. These findings establish a clear link between surface mesoscale morphology, oxidation dynamics, and catalytic function, highlighting the need for controlled surface/chemical state engineering in CO2RR catalysts. These insights offer practical guidance…

shortlist.title: What if we were to design transport in aqueous electrolytes using learnings from lithium battery research?
shortlist.abstract: Electrolyte design has played a crucial role in the development of lithium batteries for a range of applications. Of late, there is a renewed interest in developing a new generation of aqueous batteries to cheaply store energy for the grid. Given the amount of research our community has carried out developing lithium electrolytes, an intriguing possibility is to leverage these learnings to accelerate the development of aqueous electrolytes - especially when battery development requires decades of effort. We herein examine this argument to guide aqueous battery electrolyte research. We discuss the current understanding of transport mechanisms across molecular and continuum scales that can be readily applied to advance aqueous electrolytes. Based on such multiscale understanding, we propose the concept of transport maps to quantitatively assess electrolyte advances. We additionally synthesize the aqueous electrolyte transport property measurement literature to propose bottom-up design heuristics. The discussion is intentionally confined to binary electrolytes made up of a salt dissolved in water to uncover the nature of ion-ion and ion-water interactions that can be combined to imagine new aqueous electrolytes of varying complexities.

shortlist.title: Porous materials for sulfur dioxide capture from flue gas
shortlist.abstract: This review summarizes recent advances in porous materials for SO 2 capture, compares their adsorption mechanisms and structure–performance relationships, and highlights challenges and prospects for flue gas desulfurization.

shortlist.title: Promises and pitfalls of community moderation on social media
shortlist.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
shortlist.abstract: Social media platforms have traditionally relied on internal moderation teams and partnerships with independent fact-checking organizations to identify and flag problematic content. Recently, however, platforms including X (formerly Twitter) and Meta have shifted toward community-driven content moderation by launching their own versions of crowd-sourced fact-checking—Community Notes. If effectively scaled and governed, such crowd-checking initiatives have the potential to combat misinformation as successfully as community-driven efforts once did with spam. However, moderating misinformation is inherently more complex: perceptions of truth are often shaped by personal biases, political leanings, and cultural contexts, complicating consensus on what constitutes misleading content. This suggests that community efforts, while valuable, cannot replace the indispensable role of professional fact-checkers. Here we explore the emerging role of community-driven moderation, critically evaluate both the promises and the challenges of Community Notes at scale, and identify how collaborative and technical innovations can integrate the two distinct approaches.

The moderation process is divided into two main stages: (i) Pre-Moderation using AI classifiers, which categorize content as either restricted — blocked from appearing on the platform — or less harmful , which is passed on for community moderation; and (ii) Community Moderation , where eligible volunteers may propose additional context that undergoes peer review by other contributors with diverse perspectives before being published after a consensus is achieved.

shortlist.title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO 2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
shortlist.abstract: Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO 2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady‐state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO 2 hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO 2 hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO 2 hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO 2 activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo‐ and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

shortlist.title: Single-Atom Catalysts for Biomass Valorization
shortlist.abstract: Biomass, the only renewable organic carbon resource on Earth, offers a promising feedstock for producing value-added chemicals and fuels. However, the principal challenge in biomass valorization stems from the inherent complexity of its functional groups, necessitating catalysts capable of precisely activating specific C–O/C═O/C═C bonds while suppressing undesired side reactions. Single-atom catalysts (SACs), featuring unique geometric and electronic structures as well as high atomic utilization efficiency, have shown potential for highly effective biomass conversion in thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. Drawing upon recent continuous efforts on SACs in biomass valorization, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances in applying SACs to the transformation of main components of lignocellulosic biomass and their platform molecules. Structure–activity relationships and catalytic behavior of SACs under different external stimuli (e.g., thermal, electrical, and photonic) are emphasized, showcasing their innovative applications. The important factors governing catalytic activity and selectivity with a particular focus on the geometric and electronic structures of active sites are discussed, aiming to derive fundamental principles for the rational design of efficient and selective catalysts for biomass valorization. Finally, an outlook highlights the key challenges and prospects in this flourishing field.

shortlist.title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia
shortlist.abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport-0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III-independent reverse-topology budding.

shortlist.title: Injured locusts heal or are cannibalized depending on levels of a bacterial odour molecule
shortlist.abstract: When migratory locusts are injured, an odorous chemical produced by bacteria living in or on their bodies activates the immune system, helping them to fight disease-causing agents. However, when a wound is large and the chemical becomes too concentrated, it attracts cannibalistic locusts. At low levels, guaiacol promotes immune function; at high levels, it prompts other locusts to eat their swarm-mate.

shortlist.title: Symmetry-Guided Prediction of Magnetic-Ordered Ground States
shortlist.abstract: Given the scarcity of experimentally confirmed magnetic structures, the reliable prediction of magnetic ground states is crucial yet remains a long-sought challenge due to the complex magnetic potential energy landscape. Here, we propose a symmetry-guided framework that systematically generates realistic magnetic configurations without requiring any experimental input or prior assumptions such as propagation vectors. The framework incorporates the recently developed oriented spin space group formalism, which captures symmetry-breaking pathways induced by both magnetic ordering and spin-orbit coupling. By performing nonrelativistic and relativistic first-principles calculations, we further establish the energy ladder of the generated magnetic configurations. Exemplified by three prominent unconventional magnets MnTe, Mn 3 Sn , and CoNb 3 S 6 , we demonstrate that only a few dozen first-principles calculations are sufficient to identify the ground-state magnetic structure. To demonstrate the universality and robustness of our approach, we conduct large-scale benchmark tests on the MAGNDATA database. Our framework successfully reproduces experimentally reported magnetic structures for 73% of the surveyed materials. Furthermore, in a high-throughput first-principles benchmark involving 305 compounds, 82% of experimentally reported magnetic geometries are accurately captured within an energy tolerance of 5 meV per magnetic atom from the computed ground state. Beyond reproducing known magnetic configurations, our framework further predicts a variety of low-energy metastable phases, including altermagnets, spin-orbit magnets, and noncollinear antiferromagnets with spin splitting or geometric Hall effect. shortlist.title: Universal spectral correlations in open Floquet systems with localized leaks
shortlist.abstract: We investigate how non-Hermitian random-matrix universality emerges in a physical Floquet system with localized leakage. As a concrete example, we consider the leaky quantum standard map (L-QSM) of the kicked rotor. Since the closed map exhibits circular orthogonal ensemble (COE) statistics, we compare its spectral properties with those of the truncated circular orthogonal ensemble (TCOE), which models localized leakage by removing columns from a COE matrix and thus provides the natural finite-dimensional random-matrix benchmark for the open system. The local spectral correlations of the L-QSM and TCOE show excellent agreement, exhibiting a crossover from the COE limit, recovered only when the truncation is smaller than one full column, to the universal statistics of the non-Hermitian symmetry class A I † , reached when the number of truncated columns is n L ≳ 100 , essentially independently of the matrix sizes N studied. This shows that the crossover is controlled by the number of truncated columns, n L , rather than by the physical size of the leak, Δ q = n L / N . In contrast, the global spectral properties follow a different crossover. At intermediate leakage, the L-QSM and TCOE retain an accumulation of long-lived resonances near the unit circle and remain far from the Ginibre circular law. The L-QSM additionally exhibits system-specific features, with an excess of very short-lived resonances and phase-space stickiness affecting long-lived resonances. Only at strong leakage does the TCOE density of states approach the circular law, suggesting the same limiting behavior for the L-QSM. Our results show that local bulk correlations reach non-Hermitian universality at weaker leakage than global spectral properties, which retain system-specific features over a broader…

shortlist.title: Rules-and-facts model for simultaneous generalization and memorization in neural networks
shortlist.abstract: A key capability of modern neural networks is their capacity to simultaneously learn underlying rules and memorize specific facts or exceptions. Yet, theoretical understanding of this dual capability remains limited. We introduce the Rules-and-Facts (RAF) model, a minimal solvable setting that enables precise characterization of this phenomenon by bridging two classical lines of work in the statistical physics of learning: the teacher-student framework for generalization and Gardner-style capacity analysis for memorization. In the RAF model, a fraction 1 − ε of training labels is generated by a structured teacher rule, while a fraction ε consists of unstructured facts with random labels. We characterize when the learner can simultaneously recover the underlying rule - allowing generalization to new data - and memorize the unstructured examples. Our results quantify how overparameterization enables the simultaneous realization of these two objectives: sufficient excess capacity supports memorization, while regularization and the choice of kernel or nonlinearity control the allocation of capacity between rule learning and memorization. Experiments on a CIFAR10-based RAF task show that the qualitative trade-off persists for fixed kernels, whereas representations learned by deeper neural networks substantially mitigate it, preserving factual recall while improving generalization. The RAF model provides a theoretical foundation for understanding how modern neural networks can infer structure while storing rare or non-compressible information.

shortlist.title: Taxing Homeowners Who Can't or Won't Borrow
shortlist.abstract: Using high-frequency administrative data covering millions of US homeowners, I document three novel facts about homeowner responses to property tax increases driven by rising home values. First, non-migrating homeowners cut consumption, exhibit financial distress, and do not borrow against their higher home values. Second, heterogeneity analysis shows that consumption responses do not vary by liquidity, consistent with savings target behavior. In contrast, distress responses are concentrated among liquidity-constrained homeowners. Many homeowners report being debt averse and therefore unwilling to borrow in order to avoid illiquidity and distress. Third, tax hikes induce migration—partly by displacing illiquid homeowners—but do not accelerate neighborhood change. A simple welfare framework reveals that the largest costs of property taxes arise from financial distress, suggesting welfare gains from policies that limit taxes for liquidity-constrained households.

shortlist.title: Diagnosing the Effects of Spectroscopic Training Set Imperfection on Photometric Redshift Performance
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Most LSST extragalactic science will rely on photometric redshifts (photo-z) to extract distance information for the galaxies. However, an incomplete or non-representative training set can introduce bias into photo-z estimation. It is necessary to understand how various forms of training set imperfection, such as incompleteness and non-trivial spectroscopic target selection, affect photo-z estimation algorithms, and to identify metrics best-suited to quantify the impact. This work aims to systematically study metrics for diagnosing how various photo-z methods react to certain types of training set incompleteness and non-representativeness. We use methods available through the open-source Python library Redshift Assessment Infrastructure Layers (RAIL) to systematically test the algorithms CMNN, GPz, FlexZBoost, and PZFlow on mock training data degraded in accordance with several existing spectroscopic sky surveys, as well as under conditions of inverse redshift incompleteness, which approximately mimics observed patterns of incompleteness at high redshift. We employ the algorithm TrainZ as a control. Finally, we quantify photo-z algorithm performance using a variety of statistical metrics implemented externally to RAIL. We determine that the Kullback-Liebler Divergence, Wasserstein Distance, and Probability Integral Transform are particularly informative metrics with which to assess the impact of training set imperfection on algorithmic performance. We also find that inverse redshift incompleteness effects alone lack the complexity to realistically represent anticipated training data.

shortlist.title: How Sociotropic Aesthetic Judgments Drive Opposition to Dense Housing Development
shortlist.abstract: Voter opposition to dense housing development contributes to America’s housing shortage. Prevailing explanations emphasize homeowner self-interest and “NIMBYism.” We develop a theory of how sociotropic aesthetic judgments shape housing policy preferences and demonstrate its unique implications with a series of descriptive studies and experiments. First, people who choose to live in dense neighborhoods have an aesthetic taste for density, leading homeowners in already-dense areas to be more supportive of dense development both in their neighborhoods and elsewhere. Second, voters are more supportive of dense development when it is proposed in already-dense neighborhoods where it “fits”—even voters who live in those same dense neighborhoods. Finally, genuine aesthetic distaste for tall buildings is widespread and causally affects support for development. Our findings offer a new lens for understanding housing policy preferences and suggest novel solutions for addressing America’s housing shortage.

shortlist.title: Limits of Disclosure in Search Markets
shortlist.abstract: This paper examines competitive information disclosure in search markets with a mix of selective consumers, who search costlessly, and casual consumers, who incur positive search costs. Selective consumers incentivize truthful disclosure; casual consumers, concealment. With both types, the equilibrium features partial disclosure, which persists despite intense competition. Casual consumers may search actively, but only in small markets. While selective consumers benefit from increased competition, casual consumers may be harmed. Changes in search costs have non-monotone effects: the equilibrium approaches full disclosure as the cost approaches zero or the mean valuation. When costs are high, further increases raise equilibrium informativeness and the welfare of selective consumers, while reducing the welfare of casual consumers.

shortlist.title: Gut-bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells contribute to HIV persistence during ART
shortlist.abstract: Antigen specificities of most HIV reservoir cells remain poorly defined. We examined whether CD4 + T cells specific for gut bacterial antigens contribute to HIV replication and persistence. Gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells were markedly reduced in viremic people living with HIV (PWH) and remained incompletely restored despite antiretroviral therapy (ART), with those expressing markers of HIV permissiveness being preferentially depleted. Circulating gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells from PWH on ART displayed lower TCR β diversity and persistent functional disruption, characterized by attenuation of canonical effector programs and a higher proportion of cells with cytotoxic features. By contrast, rectum-localized bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells from the same individuals exhibited a tolerogenic profile, highlighting the compartment-specific function of these cells. Near-full-length proviral sequencing revealed clonal expansions of HIV genomes within circulating gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells from ART-treated participants, with evidence of cross-reactivity across multiple bacterial species. Genetically intact proviruses were enriched in Salmonella Typhimurium-specific CD4 + T cells. These findings suggest that gut-bacteria-specific CD4 + T cells are preferentially targeted during untreated HIV infection and incompletely restored by ART, harboring genetically intact HIV genomes and constituting an antigen-driven reservoir in which chronic stimulation by gut microbial antigens promotes clonal proliferation and long-term HIV persistence during ART.

shortlist.title: Revisiting the enigmatic sixth star cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: The Fornax dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy is one of only two Local Group dSphs that host a population of globular star clusters (GCs), the present-day properties of which have often been used to investigate the nature of the dark matter. An additional overdensity of stars called Fornax 6, lying at a projected distance of ~0.3 kpc from the galaxy centre, was recently identified as a sixth GC residing in Fornax. However, this conclusion was based on relatively shallow photometric observations and a limited number of spectra. Here, we reinvestigate the nature of Fornax 6 by analysing MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations alongside deep GMOS-S imagery. Using a sample of 131 spectra of red giant and red clump stars, we confirm the Fornax 6 overdensity as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with respect to the surrounding field population. Specifically, we identify 43 likely members associated with the cluster, from which we measure [Fe/H] = −0.63 ± 0.03 dex, vₗₒₛ = 50.8^(+0.8)_(-0.7) km s⁻¹, and σ ᵥ = 3.3^(+1.4)_(-1.9) km s⁻¹. The main-sequence turn-off, observed here for the first time, strongly suggests that these stars are coeval and well described by a ~3 Gyr old isochrone. The cluster is characterised by an irregular morphology, a large half-light radius (Rₕ=8.8^(+1.1)_(-1.3)pc), a small flattening (e < 0.26, 68% upper limit), and low luminosity (MV = −5.0 ± 0.4). Our improved characterisation of Fornax 6 supports its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax’s unique GC system.

shortlist.title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
shortlist.abstract: Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl interface increases the discharge current at which voiding commences tenfold, from 0.2 to 2 mA cm −2 at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm −2 at 30 °C and 8 mA cm −2 at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

shortlist.title: MIDIS: Strong H β +[O iii ] Line Emitters at z ≳ 9
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We search for strong Hβ+[O iii] line emitters at z = 9.4 − 11.3 in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field using ultra-deep MIRI/F560W imaging from the MIRI Deep Imaging Survey. Three galaxies show F560W flux excesses relative to their continuum, consistent with Hβ+[O iii] emission. We derive rest-frame Hβ+[O iii] equivalent widths of EW^(Hβ+[OIII])ᵣₑₛₜ ≃ 700-1500Å, placing them among the most extreme nebular line emitters at this epoch. Combining our sources with 15 spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at z > 9 with published Hβ+[O iii] measurements, we derive a median EW^(Hβ+[Oiii])ᵣₑₛₜ = 1433Å with median absolute deviation of 670 Å. We find no evidence for an increase or decline in EW^(Hβ+[O_III])ᵣₑₛₜ at z > 9. Binning the combined z > 9 sample by UV luminosity, we find higher equivalent widths in more UV-luminous systems. While consistent with trends at z = 6 − 9, the difference is not significant, and subject to heterogeneous sample selection. No significant anti-correlation between Hβ+[O iii] equivalent width and stellar mass is found, although a fit suggests a trend consistent with lower-redshift observations. We place a first constraint on the Hβ+[O iii] line luminosity function at z ≃ 9 − 11 (Φ ∼ 10−3.3 Mpc−3 dex−1 at log (L_(Hβ+[Oᵢii])/ erg s⁻¹) = 42.45) consistent with a decline relative to z ≃ 7 − 8. We derive ionising photon production efficiencies of log (ξion/Hz erg−1) = 25.3 − 25.5, and find tentative trends between ξion and EW^(Hβ+[O_III])ᵣₑₛₜ, and between ξion and β, consistent with those observed at z = 6 − 9. These results suggest that the physical conditions governing nebular emission and its link to the UV continuum are in place at z > 9.

shortlist.title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
From Design to Disclosure
shortlist.abstract: We study the role of hard information in contractual and market settings in which the receiver can flexibly adjust allocations and transfers in response to the sender's disclosure. These settings include monopoly pricing, insurance contracting, and policy negotiations. Across these settings, the sender is worst off if she reveals her type completely because the receiver would then adjust the terms of trade to extract her surplus. Taking this feature as our central departure from the literature, we characterize the entire set of equilibrium payoffs in these disclosure games. We prove an equivalence result: a payoff profile can be approximated by an equilibrium of the disclosure game if and only if it can be achieved through information design. Thus, there exist equilibria in which the sender obtains approximately her commitment payoff.

shortlist.title: Optimal Incentive Design for Decentralized Dynamic Matching Markets
shortlist.abstract: In decentralized dynamic matching markets, agents can benefit from sharing resources, but they will collaborate only if properly incentivized. Motivated by applications such as multihospital kidney exchanges and job-hunting markets, this paper proposes novel monetary and nonmonetary mechanisms to incentivize collaboration in such decentralized dynamic markets. We study a model in which multiple self-interested agents manage local multiway dynamic matching problems. Jobs of different types arrive stochastically at each agent, expire after a limited time, and yield rewards when matched. An agent’s job backlog and actions are the agent’s private information, and each agent aims to maximize its long-run average matching reward. We design simple mechanisms that incentivize agents to submit all jobs upon arrival, thereby enabling centralized matching. Our first mechanism, the marginal-value (MV) mechanism, reimburses agents based on the MV of their submitted jobs. This can be implemented in a nonmonetary way by randomly selecting an agent (with a specified probability) to perform a match and collect the associated matching reward. We show that under the MV mechanism, full job submission constitutes an approximate Nash equilibrium—that is, the gain from unilateral deviation vanishes as the number of agents grows. To further eliminate incentives for deviation, we propose a refined mechanism, the MV-plus-credit (MVC) mechanism, and show that, when the number of agents exceeds a constant threshold, full job submission constitutes a stronger oblivious equilibrium. Numerical experiments based on kidney exchange data demonstrate that the gains from deviation under our mechanisms are small even in moderately sized markets. shortlist.title: One year of broadband radio monitoring of the enigmatic transient GRB 250702B reveals the evolution of the relativistic jet
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We present an extensive radio monitoring campaign of the unique extragalactic transient GRB 250702B, associated with unprecedentedly long duration gamma-ray emission, lasting over 3 hr. Our observations span 0.65–233 GHz from 6–356 d (observer frame) post-discovery. The radio emission shows a smoothly evolving peaked synchrotron spectrum consistent with an adiabatic shock expanding into a stratified ambient medium (ne∝R−k; k = 1.5 − 2). We detect significant variability in the low frequency (≤3 GHz) light curves which we interpret as interstellar scintillation, placing an approximate bound on the blast wave image size of 1.2 × 1016 ≲ R⊥ ≲ 5 × 1017 cm. The temporal evolution of the flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies suggest the shock that powers the radio emission is potentially a wide-angle θj ≳ 15 deg, low Lorentz factor (Γ ≲ 10) jet, or a narrow θj ≲ 2 deg (Γ0 > 50) highly relativistic jet. A narrow jet is expected for a stellar-mass black hole engine, such as a helium star merger, and the beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is consistent with the known distribution for long GRBs (EK ~ 1051 erg). The wide-angle jet scenario would instead require a progenitor involving prolonged accretion. We derive and show an intermediate or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event are viable possibilities. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is on the low end of the known distribution for relativistic SMBH TDEs (EK ~ 1050 erg). We disfavour an SMBH TDE due to lack of compatibility with the observed timescales. The detection of a jet shut off within the next year would favour a WD-IMBH TDE due to the shorter theoretical duration of super-Eddington accretion than the main-sequence TDE channels.

shortlist.title: Do Fund Managers’ Commitments to Responsible Investing Affect Private Information Acquisition, Information Environment, and Corporate Sustainability?
shortlist.abstract: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. After committing to responsible investing (via United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI)), fund managers increase private information acquisition activities, that is, corporate site visits, particularly focusing on environmental and social issues. These visits generate negligible private investment value for the visiting funds. However, the information environment at the stock level improves following these visits with lower consensus analyst forecast errors. In addition to the information production role of these visits, they also generate positive externalities for other stakeholders through incremental improvements in the sustainability practices of the firms receiving sustainability-focused site visits from UNPRI fund managers. Collectively, the paper highlights the private costs and social benefits of responsible investing. This paper was accepted by Will Cong, finance. Funding: S. Agarwal and J. shortlist.title: Corporate Contributions to Ballot Measure Campaigns: Real Effects and Valuation
shortlist.abstract: We analyze novel data on corporate contributions to ballot initiatives at the U.S. state level. Firms make large contributions to ballot measure campaigns in favor of or against specific initiatives. They contribute significantly more to business initiatives compared with ideological initiatives. Corporate campaign spending is systematically associated with the likelihood that a ballot measure passes. Contributing firms experience changes in sales growth following the passage of important ballot measures. Following successful (failed) initiatives, all firms in affected industries exhibit significantly more positive (negative) cumulative abnormal returns around the election, but contributing firms do more so than peers. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Funding: R. Fahlenbrach gratefully acknowledges financial support from the Swiss Finance Institute. shortlist.title: Autoantibodies against Type I Interferons and Death from H7N7 Avian Influenza
Diverse lung challenges elicit a conserved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation blueprint
shortlist.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b + mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

shortlist.title: Conserved T cell receptor usage underpins recognition of CD1c presenting a mycobacterial lipid
shortlist.abstract: The mechanism by which αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) recognize mycobacterial lipids presented by CD1 family members is not well understood. We used CD1c tetramers loaded with the mycobacterial phosphomycoketide (PM) or mannosyl-PM to isolate T cells from healthy blood donors and individuals from a tuberculosis (TB)-endemic region of South Africa, with higher frequencies observed in individuals from the TB-endemic region. High-throughput analysis of >200 paired CD1c–mycoketide tetramer+ αβTCRs identified a conserved TCR motif, encoded by TRBV4-1 or TRBV7-9 variable region genes in greater than half of TCRs sequenced. A cryo-EM structure of a TRBV7-9+ TCR in complex with CD1c-PM demonstrated that the TCR bound to the A′-side of CD1c, directly contacting the phospholipid antigen and F′-portal residues. Analysis of multiple T cell clones interacting with CD1c mutants suggested that this TCR docking mode is representative of the larger TRBV7-9+ T cell population. Collectively, this study provides insight into mycobacterial lipid antigen recognition by αβ T cells restricted to CD1c.

shortlist.title: Aspiring to a Better Future: Can a Simple Psychological Intervention Reduce Poverty?
shortlist.abstract: Do higher aspirations for the future motivate people living in poverty to make long-term investments? Do their aspirations increase when economic conditions improve? To answer these questions, we run a 415-village field experiment with 8,300 women living in poverty in rural Kenya. We design an 80-minute workshop to help people set higher aspirations and plan to achieve them. We cross-randomise this with large unconditional cash transfers. The workshop substantially raises aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue, and living standards 17 months later, relative to a placebo workshop. Increases in aspirations are the most likely mechanism to explain the economic effects. Cash transfers also raise aspirations, which might help to explain why transfers increase labour supply and investment. We conclude that aspirations respond to both economic and psychological interventions, contribute to investment decisions and living standards, and are important considerations for development policy.

shortlist.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

shortlist.title: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias. Observations: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing…

shortlist.title: Right Ventricular Reverse Remodeling Without Pulmonary Vascular Unloading During Sotatercept Therapy: An Invasive Pressure–Volume Loop Study
shortlist.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading. METHODS: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure–volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography). RESULTS: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34–67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0–65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0–42.0] mm Hg; P <0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P <0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183–242] to 160 [IQR, 129–204] mL; P <0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6–56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2–44.4] g; P <0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P =0.002). Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
shortlist.abstract: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. The combination of a sensor suite, estimators, and a low-level controller achieved centimeter-scale positional flight accuracy. In addition, we developed a hierarchical controller in which a human operator provides high-level commands to direct the robot's motion. In a 30-second flight experiment conducted outside a motion-capture system, the robot avoided obstacles and ultimately landed on a sunflower. This level of sensing and computational autonomy represents a notable advancement for the aerial microrobotics community, opening further opportunities to explore onboard planning and power autonomy.

CAR-T Targeting of Mutant Calreticulin Selectively Eradicates Myeloproliferative Neoplasm-Sustaining Stem Cells
shortlist.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) arise from and are sustained by hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that acquire a driver mutation. Existing therapies fail to eliminate MPN HSCs, leaving allogeneic HSC transplantation (HSCT) as the only curative option. However, allogeneic HSCT non-selectively ablates both healthy and MPN HSCs, requiring donor stem-cell replacement and risking serious toxicities and death. MPN driver mutations in calreticulin (CALRmut) generate a shared C-terminal neopeptide unique to MPN cells that must be displayed at the cell surface in complex with the thrombopoietin receptor MPL to drive oncogenic signaling. These features make CALRmut an attractive target for selective immunotherapy. However, it is unknown whether MPN HSCs consistently display surface CALRmut to enable selective elimination in vivo via CALRmut targeting. We generated hAB2, a high-affinity CALRmut-specific humanized antibody, to use as the binding domain for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. We show that functional murine and human MPN HSCs express surface CALRmut that is reliably detected by AB2 in vitro and in vivo. We developed an MPN patient-derived tumor xenograft (PDTX) model to enable rigorous testing of human MPN HSC-directed therapies in vivo. hAB2 CAR-T cells selectively eliminate CALRmut MPN HSCs in PDTX, eradicating all detectable MPN-propagating function in serial transplantation assays, while preserving co-existing normal human and host hematopoiesis. These findings establish cell-surface CALRmut display as a therapeutically exploitable feature of MPN HSCs and support the feasibility of CALRmut-targeted, transplant-free immunotherapies with curative intent for CALRmut MPNs.

shortlist.title: Hepatic stellate cells remodel liver-resident CD8+ T cells and constrain immunosurveillance
shortlist.abstract: The liver constitutes a distinct immunological niche in which CD8+ T cells balance immune protection and tissue integrity. How chronic liver disease (CLD) remodels human liver–resident CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) create immunoinstructive fibrotic niches that regulate liver-resident CD8+ T cell differentiation, localization, and function. CD103-expressing liver-resident CD8+ T cells accumulate with increasing fibrosis severity and preferentially localize within collagen-rich scar tissue. HSC-derived and matrix-retained TGFβ promote acquisition of a residency program characterized by upregulation of CD103, ECM-binding integrins, and adhesion molecules. Despite their increased abundance, liver-resident CD8+ T cells in CLD exhibit impaired antigen-dependent effector function, increased inhibitory receptor expression, and a transcriptional program associated with T cell dysfunction. Importantly, responses to PMA/ionomycin remain intact, indicating preserved effector competence. Mechanistically, HSCs directly suppress antigen-specific liver-resident CD8+ T cell function, with partial restoration following PD-L1/PD-L2 blockade. These findings identify the fibrotic niche as a central regulator of liver-resident CD8+ T cells and reveal how fibrosis can limit local immunosurveillance.

shortlist.title: Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered ILC2s for targeted immune regulation
shortlist.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering has transformed cellular immunotherapies, yet whether CAR signaling can direct innate lymphoid cell functions for therapeutic applications has not been established. IL-10-producing ILC2s (ILC2 10 ) suppress pathogenic T cell responses in preclinical transplant models, making them attractive candidates for engineered regulatory cell therapies. Here we show that CD28 and CD3z are endogenous signaling modules with distinct expression kinetics in ILC2 activation. We engineered human ILC2 10 with CARs incorporating these domains and demonstrate that CAR activation via CD3z, CD28 or both induces robust proliferation and cytokine production, with each domain inducing distinct transcriptional programs, and combined CD3z and CD28 signaling uniquely inducing cytotoxic programs. In a xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease model, CAR-ILC2 10 more effectively inhibited human T cell engraftment and activity, displayed enhanced persistence and trafficked to sites of T cell-mediated injury. These findings establish CAR-ILC2s as programmable cellular therapies, with CAR signaling architecture shaping distinct ILC2 effector programs.

fundamentals.title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
fundamentals.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft matter physics is to describe materials, such as the living cytoplasm and tissues, that are simultaneously active, chemically driven, and exhibit long-lasting memory of mechanical stresses. Here, we construct a generalized hydrodynamic framework at finite wave vectors and frequencies that is applicable to nonequilibrium fluids with memory. By leveraging stationary correlation identities, we derive a generalized linear response theory for nonequilibrium steady states. This framework serves as a formal extension of Onsager’s regression hypothesis beyond thermal equilibrium. Our approach provides a direct pathway to derive transport coefficients from steady-state fluctuations without the traditional Mori-Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, generalizing the Green-Kubo relations to nonequilibrium systems. As a corollary, we derive two model-free variants of the nonequilibrium fluctuation-response relation for non-Markovian dynamics. These generalized relations explicitly capture the nonequilibrium circulating currents—an out-of-equilibrium signature that is invisible to conventional scalar formulations or frameworks that treat degrees of freedom independently. Applying our theory to chemically driven active fluids reveals the emergence of active viscoelastic memory, wherein chemical reaction cycles dynamically renormalize the macroscopic viscous response. Strikingly, this active memory can induce negative storage modulus at finite frequencies, a behavior absent in ordinary viscoelastic fluids. Our first-principles framework rigorously extends linear rheology to nonequilibrium systems and provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian dynamics across a broad range of biological and synthetic active matter.

fundamentals.title: Origin of Electride States and Their Responses under Pressure
fundamentals.abstract: Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. While existing theoretical frameworks, including the interstitial quasi-atom (ISQ) and electron-ion interaction (EII) models, have provided some useful phenomenological interpretations of the electride formation, the atomistic origin and the underlying physics of this charge redistribution remain unclear. Here, within a first-principles framework, we systematically study the evolution of electronic structures of compressed materials, using alkali metals as representative examples. By mapping symmetry-resolved electronic band states onto atomic orbitals, we find that (i) pressure-induced quantum confinement raises the energies of atomic orbitals due to enhanced kinetic energy and increased overlap between valence and core electrons, with the energy shift being larger for more delocalized s orbital than for more localized p and d orbitals; and (ii) this effect causes reordering of band states, making the electride states, which are composed of the interatomic hybridized pd orbitals, to progressively shift in energy below the s orbital states, leading to their occupation and the onset of electride behavior. This microscopic electronic-state picture clarifies the origin of the electride formation and provides a general framework for understanding the evolution of interstitial electronic states under compression across diverse materials.

fundamentals.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
fundamentals.abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. To examine the present scheme, we analyze the MAGNDATA database and find that 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. When the k index is fixed to its experimental value, the number of magnetic structures generated is on average about nine, also demonstrating the high efficiency of this scheme. Next, to quantitatively assess computational and predictive performance, we perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. The characteristic energy scale among oriented SSA structures is only approximately 0.29 meV per magnetic atom, about 300…

fundamentals.title: Revealing temperature effects on sliding friction through many-body phonon dynamics
fundamentals.abstract: Despite centuries of research into friction through classical mechanics, the fundamental principles governing friction remain poorly understood, particularly its temperature-dependent nature. This study proposes a quantum theory that reexamines the fundamental principles of tribology. By employing the Feynman diagrammatic perturbation technique within the framework of quantum many-body theory, this study incorporates phonon-phonon interactions to capture the microscopic mechanisms of energy dissipation. The results demonstrate that the phonon radiation governed by harmonic interactions dominates energy dissipation at cryogenic temperatures. As temperature rises, phonon scattering governed by anharmonic interactions overtakes radiation as the primary dissipation mechanism. Further increases in temperature lead to greater damping and suppressed phonon excitation, thereby reducing energy dissipation. The competition among phonon radiation, phonon scattering, and phonon excitation gives rise to the non-monotonic temperature characteristics of friction. Notably, this non-monotonic temperature dependence is also reproduced by classical molecular dynamics simulations. This framework provides a unified understanding of disparate friction trends with temperature observed across different materials, offering insights into the fundamental mechanisms of frictional energy dissipation.

fundamentals.title: Ordering of oxygen atoms in titanium revealed by superresolution electron ptychography
fundamentals.abstract: Interstitial atoms such as oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen are common point defects in crystalline solids and play important roles in determining electronic and mechanical properties. For decades, their behavior has been modeled assuming random spatial distributions owing to the lack of direct experimental access to their atomic-scale arrangements. Here, using oxygen-doped α-titanium as a model system, we overcome this fundamental limitation by achieving the first three-dimensional visualization, quantitative counting, and sub-[˚]Angstr¨om positioning of individual interstitial oxygen atoms in the bulk, enabled by super-resolution 4D-STEM ptychography with an adaptive prop agator. We find that interstitial oxygen atoms do not distribute randomly; instead, they exhibit correlated occupancy along the [0001] direction, giving rise to nanoscale ordered domains that are not detectable by conventional imaging. This discovery overturns the long-standing paradigm of randomness in interstitial systems and provides a microscopic foundation for understanding anomalous transport, strengthening, and phase stability in interstitial-engineered materials. Our approach establishes a general platform for atomic-scale defect metrology, opening avenues to ratio nally design materials through precise control of interstitial architectures in metals, semiconductors, and quantum solids.

fundamentals.title: First Principles Magnetohydrodynamical Theory for the Expanding Box Model: Effects on Expansion-induced Alfvén Wave Reflection
fundamentals.abstract: The expanding box model (EBM) has been widely employed to simulate multiscale plasma phenomena in the expanding solar wind by transforming the MHD equations to a comoving, noninertial frame. However, traditional formulations have suffered from historical ambiguity regarding the physical separation between the comoving and inertial reference frames, primarily arising from a classical approximation of an invariant magnetic field between them. To resolve this inconsistency, we reformulate the EBM from first principles using a fully covariant approach. Here, we model the expanding solar wind frame as an anisotropic expanding spacetime metric, allowing us to incorporate radial acceleration profiles and differential transverse expansion, ensuring that all physical fields are correctly transformed by expansion. We demonstrate that asymmetries identified in previous EBM-MHD literature are direct consequences of neglecting the tensorial scaling of the magnetic field. Our covariant treatment eliminates these residues, restoring symmetry in the comoving frame. Projecting our system back into the inertial frame clarifies the distinction between local plasma dynamics and plasma expansion, revealing the anisotropy of the Parker spiral as a geometric projection. Furthermore, linear wave analysis using Elsässer variables reveals that plasma expansion induces a low-frequency cutoff and geometric damping. Numerical integration demonstrates that expansion drives the reflection of Alfvén waves, generating counter-propagating modes primarily at low frequencies relative to the expansion rate, while high frequencies converge to the WKB approximation. This provides a consistent foundation for simulations, establishing that expansion can serve as a source of counter-propagating waves…

fundamentals.title: Unramified Gromov–Witten and Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Mathematical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov–Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar–Vafa invariants for Fano curve classes and primitive Calabi–Yau classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar–Vafa invariants in these cases.

fundamentals.title: The Huang–Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
fundamentals.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin 1/2 1 / 2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.

fundamentals.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
fundamentals.abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain’s proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is, for example, 1,2^(1/3),2^(-1/3) 1 , 2 1 / 3 , 2 − 1 / 3 . This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature (2,2) ( 2 , 2 ) . The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature (3,3) ( 3 , 3 ) in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on SL(2,Z)³ SL(2, R)³ SL ( 2 , Z ) 3 ∖ SL ( 2 , R ) 3 over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner’s measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

fundamentals.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits
fundamentals.abstract: We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits for orthogonal polynomials associated to a fixed measure on the real line and related systems. One of our results is that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has sine kernel asymptotics at a point ξ ξ , with regularly varying scaling, if and only if the orthogonality measure (spectral measure) has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is the Lebesgue measure. All previously known cases of sine kernel asymptotics, with absolutely continuous or singular measures, have regularly varying scaling. Our work is not limited to bulk universality; we show that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has a regularly varying scaling limit with a nontrivial limit kernel if and only if the orthogonality measure has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is not a point mass. The possible limit kernels correspond to homogeneous de Branges spaces; in particular, this equivalence completely characterizes several prominent universality classes such as hard edge universality, Fisher–Hartwig singularities, and jump discontinuities in the weights. A key ingredient in the proof is a new correspondence between measures and chains of de Branges spaces, not between Weyl functions and Hamiltonians. In order to handle limits with power law weights, this correspondence goes beyond the more common setting of Poisson-finite measures, and allows arbitrary power bounded measures.

fundamentals.title: The Limit of Nature: Thucydides and the Politics of Theory
fundamentals.abstract: This article reconsiders Thucydides’s role as a foundational theorist of human nature. Contrary to conventional readings, I argue that Thucydides approaches “nature” ( physis ) less as a universal principle of behavior than as a site of political and theoretical investigation. By distinguishing his authorial voice from those of his speakers, I demonstrate that his analysis consistently approaches human nature as a limit concept—a baseline and boundary of human capacity that emerges in moments of existential precarity—while introducing a more nuanced set of terms to describe the habitual behaviors of political groups. By nevertheless foregrounding the more robust and determinative concept of nature in moments of contentious deliberation, Thucydides encourages reflection on the political dynamics that generate essentialist theories in public discourse. His account thus serves as a helpful point of reference for thinking about how competitive, polarizing speech affects the substantive categories of political debate and analysis, and through them political action.

fundamentals.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
fundamentals.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SIREV and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.34770/6vgh-br25 and in the supplementary materials ( M180373_SM.zip [25.7MB]). fundamentals.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
fundamentals.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks. fundamentals.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
fundamentals.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

fundamentals.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
fundamentals.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
fundamentals.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive…

fundamentals.title: Constructive Ordinal Exponentiation
fundamentals.abstract: In classical mathematics, ordinal arithmetic is well-studied; constructively, addition and multiplication are well-known. We study constructive ordinal exponentiation, where ordinals are taken to be transitive, extensional, and wellfounded orders on sets. We present a negative result showing that general constructive ordinal exponentiation is impossible, but we suggest two definitions that come close. The first definition is abstract and solely motivated by the expected equations; this works as long as the base of the exponential is positive. The second definition is based on decreasing lists and can be seen as a constructive version of Sierpiński’s definition via functions with finite support; this requires the base to have a trichotomous least element. Whenever it makes sense to ask the question, the two constructions are equivalent, allowing us to prove algebraic laws, cancellation properties, and preservation of decidability of the exponential. The core ideas do not depend on any specific constructive set theory or type theory, but a concrete computer-checked mechanization using the Agda proof assistant is given in homotopy type theory.

fundamentals.title: First-principles Turbulence-driven Deflagration-to-detonation Transition Mechanism for Near-Chandrasekhar-mass White Dwarf Progenitors
fundamentals.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decades, the canonical model for normal brightness SNe Ia used in cosmology was a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) approaching the Chandrasekhar mass ( M Ch ) as it accretes from a nondegenerate stellar companion. Previously, all models of near- M Ch SNe Ia invoked an ad hoc assumption on the critical process of detonation initiation, and could therefore be tuned to a variety of outcomes. Here, we present global 3D hydrodynamical simulations of near- M Ch progenitors, which incorporate, for the first time, a laboratory-validated ab initio mechanism for the turbulence-driven deflagration-to-detonation transition (tDDT) based on the Chapman–Jouguet deflagration criterion. The tDDT mechanism is highly efficient, leading to detonation initiation, which is prompt in comparison to most prior work. Despite spanning a factor of 6 in central ignition density and a range of qualitatively distinct ignition topologies, all models converge on nearly identical synthetic spectra at peak luminosity, spectroscopically matched to the overluminous SN 1999aa. The tDDT mechanism drives each progenitor to a common detonation configuration from diverse initial conditions, providing a physical foundation for the ignition-insensitive detonation outcomes implicit in the empirical standardizability of SNe Ia. This provides the first physically motivated, self-consistent pathway for delayed detonation in SN Ia simulations. Further work is necessary to understand how this mechanism might produce more delayed detonation initiation and potentially fail, thereby yielding Type Iax…
