fundamentals.title: Local interactions drive hyperuniform tissue coverage during development
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: In living tissues, branched cells must efficiently cover territories to perform essential functions ranging from neural signaling to immune surveillance. However, how cells collectively establish and optimize tissue-scale coverage without global regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a biophysical theory of interacting branched cells and show that coupling their growth to neighbor repulsion drives efficient tissue tiling with minimal territorial overlap. Strikingly, our model predicts that the same local mechanism progressively suppresses long-range density fluctuations during development, driving the system toward a large-scale order called hyperuniformity. We confirm these theoretical predictions on microglial patterning in the developing retina and show that in perturbation experiments with limited arbor growth, both tiling and fluctuation suppression are disrupted. Our results reveal that two seemingly distinct features of tissue organization, efficient space-filling and large-scale order, share a single dynamical origin, suggesting a general principle for robust tissue patterning.

fundamentals.title: Coverage Effects in Heterogeneous Catalysis: From Fundamental Understanding to Predictive Modeling
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
authors: Danish Uzair Bin Abdul Hamid Khan Surattee
fundamentals.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calculations suffer from vast combinatorial complexity on crowded surfaces, while machine learning methods require large training data sets and have limited physical interpretability. We reveal a physics-based linear correlation mapping complex coverage-dependent adsorption energies directly to computationally inexpensive gas-phase pairwise interactions that are evaluated via Mie potentials. This correlation is governed by bond order conservation: as surface−adsorbate interactions weaken under crowding, adsorbate−adsorbate interactions strengthen. This correlation generalizes across metal surfaces having diverse crystal facets, surface tensions, and single- and multicomponent adsorption classes (e.g., dissociative S*, N* + O*, and nondissociative CO*). This correlation predicts coverage-dependent reaction thermodynamics for NO* dissociation and for atomic-adsorbate diffusion. Coverage-dependent trends in adsorption energies of CO*/Pt(111) agree with experimental calorimetry. Ultimately, these gas-phase pairwise interactions are a descriptor for lateral interactions of atomic and structurally simple adsorbates on structurally stable metal surfaces. The generalizability and physical interpretability of this descriptor open new avenues for modeling adsorption and reaction energies on crowded metal surfaces.

fundamentals.title: Turnovers Drive Supported Metal Nanoparticle Catalyst Surface Reconstruction to Kinetically Trapped Metastable Structures
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Supported metal catalysts often operate with high adsorbate coverages that can alter nanoparticle structures as compared to the clean catalyst. Such restructuring is typically described within an equilibrium picture that assumes that nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages adopt their thermodynamically preferred state. Here, we challenge this assumption and propose that under conditions of high adsorbate coverage and fast turnovers of surface species, supported metal nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages can become kinetically trapped in metastable states. We studied CO adsorption–desorption quasi-equilibrium on Pt/γ-Al2O3 using in situ IR spectroscopy and chemisorption as a function of temperature (300–650 K), CO pressure (10–2–10–4 bar), and visible photon flux (0–2 W cm–2 440 nm photons). The adsorbed CO IR band area increases with temperature and photon flux, contrary to equilibrium predictions of decreasing coverage. Estimates of apparent Pt dispersion and CO desorption rates, along with the reversibility of IR spectral changes, support the hypothesis that when CO turnovers are faster than Pt atomic rearrangements to their equilibrium state, the catalyst is driven into metastable states. We estimate atomic rearrangements time scales of 10–1–10–3 s on CO-covered Pt nanoparticles at ∼500–600 K. Grand-canonical sampling calculations show that equilibrium Pt–CO structures cannot reproduce the experimental IR trends, implying the presence of off-equilibrium coverages, structures, or both. By matching the experimental trend, theory identifies a plausible flat, nonequilibrium free-energy region that can facilitate kinetic trapping of metastable catalyst states. These results highlight the need for theoretical and experimental approaches targeting…

fundamentals.title: Curvature-guided chiral collective organization of myoblast tissues
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Surface curvature is a fundamental geometric cue in tissue morphogenesis, yet its role in guiding collective cell organization has remained elusive. Here, we show that curvature acts as a geometric control parameter that shapes supracellular alignment and chirality while modulating myogenic differentiation in myoblast tissues. Cells cultured on curved substrates self-organize into robust helical assemblies whose handedness is set, and can be reversed, by the sign of curvature: convex fibers produce right-handed helices, whereas concave channels invert the chirality. We identify a clockwise bias in single-cell motion associated with the helical actin cytoskeleton. A minimal continuum theory coupling an effective chiral drive to curvature quantitatively captures the emergence and reversal of tissue-scale chiral alignment. On substrates with spatially varying curvature, local curvature gradients organize patterned multicellular architectures while preserving a global handedness. Curvature is also associated with myogenic state, with higher curvature linked to reduced or delayed differentiation. Together, these findings reveal how complex geometries shape the alignment, symmetry, and cellular state of living tissues.

fundamentals.title: Evolution, information content, and optimality of gene regulatory architectures
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype-phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive a maximization principle, which implies that genotype-phenotype maps will evolve to associate fit phenotypes with larger numbers of possible genotypes. Mathematically, this builds on analogies between population genetics and statistical physics, as well as optimal coding in information theory. The results are particularly interesting in the context of transcriptional regulation, where optimal values of certain parameters that determine the gene regulatory architecture can be derived even without a complete knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved. We illustrate the theory using a simplified model of transcription factor (TF) binding to cis-regulatory elements (CREs): the fraction of possible CREs across the entire genotype space that bind a given TF evolves to match the fraction of CREs under selection to bind that TF. Similar "frequency matching" results are expected to emerge generically, because selection implicitly moves the entire regulatory architecture toward a fitness maximum, determining the "replicated genotype-phenotype map" for all CREs, while it simultaneously adapts toward individually fit CREs on that map. We discuss the subtleties and limitations of the theory related to biophysical constraints and the need for mutational robustness. Last, our theory suggests a possible mathematical definition for evolvability with predictive power that can be tested in evolutionary simulations and, ultimately, in comparative genetics studies.

fundamentals.title: Self-Induced Spin Glass in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The realization of spin glasses in the absence of structural disorder remains an enduring challenge in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry. Geometrical frustration provides a route to disordered magnetism in long-range ordered crystals, yet canonical self-induced spin glass (SISG) beyond ultrapure rare-earth elements remains experimentally elusive. Here, we realize a metastable transition-metal SISG phase in MnNCN (R3̅m) via high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis, stabilizing a nonequilibrium state with enhanced magnetic competition. Magnetic measurements establish canonical spin-glass behavior, featuring a freezing temperature of 38.15 K and characteristic slowing-down dynamics, alongside a high coercivity of 1838 Oe. First-principles calculations reveal this SISG behavior is inherently rooted in the frustrated Mn triangular lattice. Mapping the energetic hierarchy uncovers strong competition among distinct antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. Crucially, high-pressure-driven anisotropic lattice compression alters the Mn-ligand orbital overlap, significantly amplifying the intralayer coupling within the ab triangular planes. This chemical–mechanical modulation intensifies the competition between intralayer and dominant interlayer couplings, producing a strongly frustrated three-dimensional magnetic network. Energy evaluations verify a profound near-degeneracy among these competing states. Rapid quenching kinetically preserves this structurally ordered metastable phase, generating the complex energy landscape characteristic of a spin glass. Electronic-structure analyses further identify the Mn–N–C–N–Mn superexchange pathway mediated by covalent [N═C═N]2– ligands as the origin of magnetic coupling, yielding an intrinsic phase robustness…

fundamentals.title: Bright Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn: A Cloud-Scale Star Formation Model Unifying Variable SFE, IMFs, and Stochasticity
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: To investigate the origins of the high abundance of UV-bright galaxies at z > 10, we present a new semi-analytic model that bridges the gap between small-scale star formation physics and large-scale galaxy evolution by explicitly tracking discrete star-forming clouds within smoothly evolving dark matter potentials. Unlike conventional semi-analytic models, our approach naturally captures the stochasticity of star formation, allowing us to isolate how cloud properties, star formation efficiencies (SFEs), and stellar initial mass functions (IMFs) shape the star-formation burstiness of early galaxies. Clouds are drawn sequentially from a cloud mass distribution, assigned an SFE and IMF depending on cloud mass, metallicity, and redshift, and evolve under the influence of short-timescale stellar feedback. We identify three distinct star formation regimes arising from the interplay between cloud masses, densities, and feedback timescales: a stochastic, feedback-limited regime in low-mass halos with long quiescent phases; a bursty regime regulated by the cloud mass distribution; and a smooth, continuous regime in massive halos. Our fiducial model adopts a dynamic IMF, an SFE linked to cloud properties and the IMF, and massive, moderately dense clouds. Varying assumptions reveals that top-heavy IMFs and enhanced SFEs in massive clouds amplify burstiness, while altering the upper cloud mass or density normalisation is secondary. Among model ingredients, the IMF most strongly impacts the UV luminosity function (LF), while switching to a constant SFE boosts the faint end, and reducing the maximum cloud mass decreases the bright end. These results demonstrate that cloud-scale physics critically shape early galaxy UV luminosity distributions.

fundamentals.title: Aristotle on the Boundaries of Processes
fundamentals.abstract: This paper challenges the dominant reading of Aristotle’s theory of the boundaries of processes, according to which he takes every interval of process to be ‘open’, excluding both the beginning and the end. Drawing on the Physics and Metaphysics, I argue that this reading is incorrect. Instead, Aristotle holds that every interval of process is half-open, excluding the end but including the beginning. He also extends this structure to intervals of rest because in both cases the end can (and must) exist without the earlier condition continuing, whereas the beginning cannot exist without the condition it initiates. The alternative reading helps improve our understanding of Aristotle’s handling of the well-known stopping and starting problem, and secures him a defensible place in both ancient and modern debates about boundaries.

food.title: “Prevalence and associated risk factors of ectoparasite infestation in Ethiopian poultry: meta-analysis”
food.abstract: Ectoparasite infestation is a major parasitic problem affecting chicken health and productivity worldwide. Despite the substantial economic impact of poultry ectoparasites, evidence on their epidemiology in Ethiopia remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of ectoparasite infestation, characterise major ectoparasite groups, and assess associated factors among chickens in Ethiopia. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2000 and 2026. Seventeen articles met the inclusion criteria, yielding 56 datasets, as some studies reported multiple ectoparasite groups. A random-effects model was used to estimate pooled prevalence while accounting for between-study heterogeneity. The overall pooled prevalence of ectoparasite infestation among chickens in Ethiopia was 63.0% (95% CI: 53.0-73.0%). In terms of region, the highest prevalence was observed in Oromia (68.0%), followed by Tigray (63.0%) and SNNPR (58.0%), whereas Amhara showed the lowest prevalence (42.0%). Among the reported ectoparasite groups, lice had the highest pooled prevalence (43.0%), followed by mites (27.0%), fleas (26.0%), mixed infestations (9.0%), and ticks (6.0%). The prevalence of ectoparasite infestation showed a slight decreasing trend over time, but the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.431). While prevalence was similar between studies with sample sizes ≤384 and >384, no significant difference was observed between the groups (p = 0.906). food.title: Carbon-smart broiler production: life-cycle hotspots, mitigation strategies, and meat-quality trade-offs
food.abstract: The poultry industry faces mounting pressure to reduce its environmental footprint while maintaining high productivity, economic viability, and superior meat quality. Although broiler production generally yields lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions than other livestock sectors, its rapid global expansion has heightened concerns over the carbon emissions associated with feed production, energy use, manure management, housing, transportation, and processing. As a result, integrated carbon-smart strategies are essential for achieving sustainable poultry systems. This review critically evaluates the primary contributors to the carbon footprint of broiler production and synthesizes current and emerging mitigation strategies that do not compromise productive performance or meat quality. We place particular emphasis on precision nutrition-including low-protein and precision-formulated diets-alternative protein sources, phytogenic feed additives, precision feeding technologies, resource-efficient housing, renewable energy integration, and circular bioeconomy approaches. Furthermore, we examine how these mitigation strategies influence key meat quality attributes, such as oxidative stability, fatty acid composition, shelf life, and sensory characteristics. Recent advances in precision livestock farming, AI-driven decision support systems, and sustainability-oriented breeding are also highlighted as promising tools for enhancing carbon efficiency. Finally, we address current challenges in carbon footprint quantification, notably methodological inconsistencies in life cycle assessments (LCA) and the lack of standardized sustainability indicators for the poultry sector. By integrating nutritional, managerial, technological, and environmental perspectives, this review proposes a…

food.title: Time-resolved multi-omics reveals sustained antiviral activation and hepatic lipid remodeling during ALV-J infection in chickens
food.abstract: Avian leukosis virus subgroup J (ALV-J) is an oncogenic retrovirus associated with persistent infection, immunosuppression, and neoplastic diseases in chickens, with the liver serving as an important target organ. However, the temporal coordination of hepatic immune and metabolic responses during the early course of ALV-J infection remains unclear. Here, we performed time-resolved proteomic and metabolomic analyses of chicken livers at 7, 14, and 21 days post-infection (dpi). Hepatic ALV-J RNA was detected throughout the observation period and was accompanied by histopathological injury and extensive immunometabolic remodeling. Antiviral and interferon-responsive proteins, including OASL, STAT1, EIF2AK2, and CMPK2, remained elevated at multiple time points. The sustained elevation of these antiviral proteins was accompanied by reductions in selected mitochondrial respiratory-chain proteins and the redox cofactors NADH and flavin mononucleotide. Lipid remodeling also became increasingly prominent over the course of infection, as reflected by the accumulation of multiple lysophospholipid species, together with decreases in phospholipid backbone-related metabolites. Based on its persistent induction and known roles in antiviral responses and mitochondrial nucleotide metabolism, CMPK2 was selected for functional analysis. ALV-J infection induced CMPK2 expression in HD11 cells. CMPK2 overexpression increased intracellular DHE fluorescence, ALV-J Env protein levels, and infectious viral titers, whereas treatment with CMPK2-targeting siRNAs reduced DHE fluorescence without significantly affecting viral replication. These findings suggest that CMPK2 contributes to infection-associated changes in DHE fluorescence in HD11 cells, while its overexpression can enhance ALV-J…

food.title: Enhanced baseline immune priming and controlled inflammation drive resistance to Salmonella Typhimurium in Lueyang Black Chicken
food.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium is an important foodborne pathogen in poultry, yet the immune mechanisms underlying natural variation in resistance to infection among chicken breeds remain poorly understood. Lueyang Black Chicken (LBC), an indigenous Chinese chicken breed, provides a model for investigating breed-related differences in immune responses to Salmonella infection, although its underlying immune characteristics remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to compare the baseline immune status and immune responses to Salmonella Typhimurium infection between LBC and Arbor Acres broilers (AA), and to explore the potential immunological basis of their differential resistance. A total of 150 LBC and 150 AA were used, and immune cell populations, immune-related gene expression, tissue histopathology, and ileal bacterial loads were assessed under physiological conditions and following Salmonella Typhimurium challenge. Compared with AA, LBC had higher blood lymphocytes, B cells as well as higher IL-10 expression under physiological conditions ( P < 0.05). Conversely, LBC exhibited significantly lower ileal TLR4 expression and hepatic pro-inflammatory factor levels ( P < 0.05). Following Salmonella Typhimurium infection, LBC exhibited a significantly lower ileal Salmonella bacterial load and fimA expression than AA after infection ( P < 0.05). Additionally, significant breed × infection interactions were observed for intestinal NLRP3 expression and SIgA levels ( P < 0.05). Following infection, AA broilers showed significant increases in ileal monocyte/macrophage counts and iNOS expression, as well as in splenic CD8α + T cells and monocyte/macrophage counts and IL-17 expression, compared with their respective control groups ( P < 0.05). food.title: Essential oils in food preservation: Integrating antimicrobial efficacy with evolutionary and microbiome selectivity considerations
authors: Eliza de Jesus Barros dos Santos
food.abstract: Background Essential oils (EOs) and their constituents (EOCs) can support food preservation, but antimicrobial efficacy alone does not characterize every surviving-cell state or community response. Minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations, colony-forming units, and shelf-life measurements remain essential; additional endpoints may be needed when exposure histories or non-target populations are relevant. Scope and approach This critical narrative review integrates foundational and recent studies on EO/EOC exposure, microbial stress responses, experimental evolution, loss of culturability, and food microbial communities. Evidence is distinguished by intervention, experimental system, exposure design, and endpoint. Laboratory and non-food findings are used for mechanistic context, with their transfer to foods explicitly limited. Key findings and conclusions Reported responses include injury, altered stress tolerance, stable resistance in selected experimental systems, cross-protection, collateral sensitivity, and viable but nonculturable (VBNC) states; other studies detected no increased tolerance under the conditions tested. Food studies also report community and metabolite changes, although relative-abundance profiles and associations seldom establish ecological causality. We propose an integrated, evolution-aware and microbiome-selective preservation perspective organized by the Microbial Fate Map, Sublethal EO Paradox, Microbiome Selectivity Index (MSI), and Evolutionary Safety Window (ESW). MSI and ESW are proposed conceptual frameworks, without validated scores or boundaries. Their value must be tested against conventional efficacy and quality endpoints in defined food systems. Evidence for bacterial adaptation is substantially stronger than evidence for…

food.title: Emerging strategies in coffee fermentation: From starter culture to synthetic microbial community
food.abstract: Background Coffee is a globally consumed beverage. After harvesting, coffee can be processed in various ways, one of which is the wet method. The conventional wet processing method involves immersing the beans in water for fermentation. Although this fermentation improves the sensory profile of the beverage, the process is generally carried out spontaneously, relying on the indigenous microbiota, which makes standardization difficult. Scope and approach This study employed a narrative review based on articles indexed in scientific databases, including Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect, covering studies published between 2022 and 2026. This study aims to critically analyze conventionally employed fermentation processes and propose the use of synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) as an emerging strategy for this process. While many studies have investigated fermentation inoculated with isolated or mixed strains (simultaneous or sequential inoculation), there is often a lack of rational design in culture development, hindering process reproducibility. Consequently, an emerging strategy involves the rational and well-structured design of microbial communities for use in coffee fermentation. Key findings and conclusion The rational development of synthetic microbial communities, integrated with multi-omics tools, is an emerging strategy for standardizing coffee fermentation and improving beverage quality. Furthermore, the use of genetically modified organisms, either for producing compounds of interest or for specific applications, represents a promising approach to further enhance the fermentation process. Overall, the use of SynComs for coffee fermentation can be considered an emerging strategy for implementation, whereas the use of genetically…

food.title: Plant-based cheese alternatives: Reframing processing strategies towards fermentation-driven innovation
food.abstract: Background The growing demand for sustainable and animal-free foods has accelerated global interest in plant-based cheese alternatives (PBCAs). Despite rapid market expansion, many commercial PBCA products still struggle to replicate the flavour, texture and functionality of dairy cheese. Key barriers include difficulty forming meltable plant protein networks, limited utilisation of plant-derived sugars by some starter cultures and a lack of suitable precursors for cheese-like flavour development. Scope and approach This review presents a process-based perspective on PBCA development by categorising current approaches into non-fermented and fermented systems. Non-fermented approaches rely mainly on functional ingredients and processing techniques to build product structure and texture, whereas fermented approaches utilise microbial metabolism to improve flavour, texture and sensory quality, with particular attention to recent advances in culture selection and adaptation. The applications and limitations of fermentation and emerging approaches, including precision fermentation, hybrid systems, multi-omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are also discussed. Key findings and conclusions Fermentation provides a promising strategy for narrowing the quality gap between plant-based and dairy cheeses. Future progress will require a better understanding of microbial adaptation to plant-based substrates and the interactions between microorganisms and plant matrices. Cultures should be evaluated in the intended cheese formulation, linking substrate utilisation and acidification with flavour and texture development. Comparisons with non-fermented controls should establish the microbial contributions, and pilot-scale trials should assess product consistency and safety. Precision…

food.title: Hydrogen-dependent sulfur and iron reduction by marine thermophiles as analogs for early Earth and ocean world processes
food.abstract: Life on the early Earth was likely anaerobic, H 2 dependent, CO 2 fixing, and thermophilic in a marine hydrothermal setting. Geochemical and mineral evidence suggests that sulfur and iron respiration occurred during the Paleoarchean (3.6–3.2 Ga). However, the predominant mechanisms of H 2 -dependent sulfur and iron respiration in hydrothermal systems, then or now, have yet to be elucidated. Studying these processes in microorganisms from modern hydrothermal systems provides context for interpreting the characteristics of life during the Paleoarchaean. All the bacteria and archaea that have been cultured and characterized as extremely thermophilic, marine, H 2 dependent, and sulfur reducing or iron reducing (36 species) were surveyed for genes related to energy generation and terminal reduction processes. Respiratory hydrogenases, Nuo-like complexes, and ATP synthases were all universally conserved. These data, coupled with phenotypic and biochemical information, suggest that these organisms oxidize H 2 outside the cytoplasmic membrane, reduce menaquinone, and generate a proton motive force for ATP synthesis. The most conserved sulfur reduction gene encoded a cytoplasmic NAD(P)H sulfur reductase. Genes encoding cytoplasmic hydrogenases and membrane-bound pyranopterin oxidoreductases were also common. The widespread conservation of menaquinol-dependent fumarate reductase points to CO 2 assimilation as another means of electron disposal, with excess reductant possibly used to drive sulfur or iron reduction. Understanding the metabolic potential of H 2 -dependent marine thermophiles deepens our knowledge of life in hydrothermal systems and contributes to the interpretation of data from ocean world missions.

food.title: Protein hydrolysates as functional supplements for serum-free media in cellular agriculture: Functions, challenges, and emerging strategies
food.abstract: Background Cellular agriculture offers a potential alternative to conventional meat production, yet the high cost and reliance on animal-derived components in cell culture media remain barriers to commercialization. Fetal bovine serum (FBS), traditionally used to support cell growth and differentiation, introduces ethical concerns, batch-to-batch variability, and high costs. Protein hydrolysates have therefore attracted attention as potential functional supplements for serum-free media. Scope and approach This review evaluates protein hydrolysates and bioactive peptides as functional components of serum-free media for cellular agriculture. We summarize their reported effects on cell proliferation and differentiation, examine the underlying molecular mechanisms and signaling pathways, and critically assess key challenges affecting their translation to cultivated meat production. We further discuss the integration of omics approaches and artificial intelligence (AI) for peptide identification, bioactivity prediction, and rational media design. Key findings Protein hydrolysates provide bioactive peptides and nutrients that can support myogenic cell proliferation and differentiation, although their effects vary with protein source, hydrolysis conditions, peptide composition, and culture environment. Key translational challenges include cell line and species specificity, scalability and bioreactor compatibility, safety and manufacturing consistency, and potential sensory impacts. In addition, limited characterization of bioactive peptides and peptide–activity datasets constrain systematic media optimization. Omics and AI approaches offer opportunities to address these limitations by linking peptide composition with cellular responses and enabling data-driven hydrolysate…

food.title: Tracking respiratory syncytial virus dynamics in wastewater during the 2024–2025 season in Switzerland
food.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is responsible for a substantial health burden worldwide, particularly among children and older adults. In 2023, novel immunoprophylactic interventions for RSV were approved, underscoring the need to monitor circulating RSV lineages and detect mutations that could compromise intervention effectiveness. Here, we implemented wastewater-based genomic RSV surveillance by integrating digital PCR and amplicon-based sequencing within Switzerland's national wastewater monitoring program. We tracked RSV subtypes and individual mutations across the 2024-2025 peak season in six Swiss cities. RSV-A and RSV-B co-circulated nationwide, and both exhibited similar epidemiological dynamics estimated from their subtype-specific effective reproduction numbers. No previously reported F protein mutations relevant to prophylaxis efficacy were identified. Genetic diversity analysis of wastewater-derived sequences reflected patterns previously reported in clinical data, with higher diversity in RSV-A than RSV-B, and greater variability in the G compared to the F gene. These findings demonstrate the potential of wastewater-based RSV surveillance for monitoring RSV dynamics and diversity and establish a national baseline for RSV evolution during the first season following vaccine implementation in Switzerland.IMPORTANCERespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory virus that can cause serious illness in vulnerable populations. The recent development of RSV immunoprophylaxis products has increased the importance of monitoring viral evolution. Standard surveillance based on clinical testing captures only a fraction of infections. food.title: Exploration of the microbial diversity and functional characteristics of traditional sourdough in Inner Mongolia
food.abstract: To explore the microbial diversity and metabolic functional characteristics of traditional sourdough in Inner Mongolia, 40 samples were analysed using culturable methods and metagenomic sequencing. A total of 353 bacterial isolates were identified and belonged to 30 genera and 50 species using culturable methods, with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum , Leuconostoc citreum , Lactococcus lactis , Pediococcus pentosaceus , and Fructilactobacillus sanfranciscensis being the dominant species. Furthermore, 225 yeast isolates belonging to 9 genera and 11 species were identified, among which Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Maudiozyma humilis were predominant. A total of 3,698 taxa across 1,114 genera were annotated using metagenomic sequencing, and the dominant species were consistent with the results obtained using the culture method. Microbial diversity analysis confirmed significant disparities in community composition between continuously back-slopped and spontaneously fermented sourdough ( p < 0.05). Successive back-slopping remarkably enriched niche-specialized, sourdough-adapted microbial taxa, whereas spontaneous fermentation maintained a more complex microbiome abundant in flour-derived plant-associated bacteria. Metagenomic functional annotation indicated that lactic acid bacteria and yeasts synergistically regulate core fermentative pathways, including carbohydrate catabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, and CO 2 generation for dough leavening. Comparative transcriptomics reveals the electrosynthesis mechanisms of Sporomusa ovata under different reduction potentials
food.abstract: Understanding the metabolic mechanism of Sporomusa ovata is crucial for the practical applications of microbial electrosynthesis systems (MESs), a promising technology to sequester CO 2 . This study aims to investigate the electrosynthesis mechanisms of S. ovata under different cathodic potentials using comparative transcriptomics. As the cathodic potential became more negative from −0.4 to −0.7 V (vs standard hydrogen electrode [SHE]), acetate synthesis in MESs increased from 0.59 ± 0.05 to 6.03 ± 0.23 mM, while electron recovery efficiency decreased from 117.7 ± 6.8% to 52.5 ± 2.4%. Transcriptional analysis revealed that H 2 -mediated indirect extracellular electron uptake may be the core mechanism of S. ovata at −0.7 and −0.4 V. At both potentials, S. ovata relied on ATP synthesis from membrane hydrogenase-dependent respiratory chains. Compared with −0.4 V, upregulation of hydABC at −0.7 V enhanced cytoplasmic hydrogenase-based reducing power, dominating CO 2 fixation via the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. Compared with −0.7 V, the transcriptional activity of membrane hydrogenase ( hupSL , hydA2B2 ) and higher expression of membrane electron transport components reflected the importance of the membrane-bound respiratory chain for S. ovata survival at −0.4 V. This work provides strategies for fine-tuning MESs to optimize energy efficiency and product specificity in sustainable biomanufacturing. Sporomusa ovata has been widely used as a cathode catalyst in MES research due to its extracellular respiratory capacity and two distinct H + -driven respiratory chains for chemolithoautotrophy. Development and behavior of Steinernema hermaphroditum nematodes are impacted by a bacterial flavin monooxygenase
food.abstract: Beneficial animal–microbe symbioses occur across the tree of life, with observable impacts on animal development and behavior. The bacterial enzyme complex HpaBC hydroxylates aromatic compounds, which may effect host neurotransmitter-dependent phenotypes. The bacterium Xenorhabdus griffiniae , a beneficial intestinal symbiont of Steinernema hermaphroditum entomopathogenic nematodes, encodes HpaBC. Computational docking of X. griffiniae HpaB substrates showed energetically favorable docking for 4-hydroxyphenylacetate and tyrosine and some affinity for dopamine. We hypothesized that Xenorhabdus HpaBC may influence nematode host development or behavior through its potential action on tyrosine degradation or dopamine catabolism. In support of this idea, we demonstrate a negative correlation between X. griffiniae hpaBC expression and body length and egg-laying behavior in adult S. hermaphroditum nematodes. Moreover, hpaBC expression is necessary for X. griffiniae bacteria to colonize the nematode intestine in the infective juvenile stage. Taken together, these findings indicate that HpaBC may be a part of the metabolic crosstalk occurring between X. griffiniae and S. hermaphroditum at multiple stages of their shared life cycle. hpaBC orthologs are widely present across bacterial phyla, including in pathogens and mutualists of plants and animals. Our findings raise the possibility that HpaBC could be a conserved mechanism by which host-associated bacteria influence physiology and behavior. food.title: Synergistic nisin–lysozyme treatment eliminates culturable cells in Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on stainless steel: a laboratory proof of concept for natural antimicrobial interventions
food.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on stainless steel persist in ready-to-eat (RTE) food production because of their tolerance to conventional disinfection. This study evaluated nisin and lysozyme, two food-grade antimicrobials, against preformed L. monocytogenes biofilms (strains A1 and M5) on type 316 stainless steel at early (48 h) and mature (5-day) stages. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) and working minimum biofilm eradication concentrations (MBEC w ; operational, assay-specific values giving no detectable culturable cells at 24 h and a ≥3-log reduction within 2 h) were determined. MBEC w /MIC ratios of 2–12 indicated biofilm-associated tolerance. Confocal microscopy showed thicker untreated biofilms at 5 days than at 48 h for M5 (27.3 to 36.0 μm) and, less clearly, for A1 (19.8 to 26.5 μm). Solid-surface checkerboard assays, expressed as Fractional Biofilm Eradication Concentration indices (FBECi), identified synergistic combinations (FBECi ≤ 0.5) that reduced counts below the detection limit (2.10 log 10 CFU/cm 2 ) within 2 h using only 6–25% (nisin) and 3–25% (lysozyme) of individual MBEC w values, a 75–97% reduction in antimicrobial usage compared with single agents. In regeneration assays, five of eight combinations showed no recovery of culturable cells within 24 h, under nutrient-rich conditions. Combined treatments reduced biomass and polysaccharide content more than single agents, compatible with, but not proof of, complementary action of lysozyme and nisin. These findings from an inert stainless-steel model suggest that nisin–lysozyme combinations warrant testing as a direct food-surface antimicrobial for RTE products, rather than as an equipment sanitiser; efficacy on biological surfaces remains to be established.

food.title: Characterization of common commercial honeys across the Mediterranean area
food.abstract: This study aimed to authenticate and characterize commercial honey samples from the Mediterranean area. Seventy-two samples spanning five botanical origins (acacia, chestnut, lavender, linden, and multifloral) from five Mediterranean countries (Croatia, France, Greece, Italy, and Spain) were evaluated through melissopalynological and sensory analysis, alongside physicochemical properties, sugars, anions, and cations. Linear models were used to assess the effects of botanical and geographical origin on studied traits, while Principal Component Analysis (PCA) allowed visualize sample clustering according to them. Approximately 47% of the samples exhibited at least one non-compliance, with botanical origin mislabeling being the most prevalent issue. Following reclassification, 51 samples were retained for further analysis. Overall, 86 nectareous taxa were identified, Smilax and Citrus emerging as potential regional markers. All physicochemical parameters met European quality standards. Electrical conductivity correlated significantly with major ionic species (ρ = 0.36, p < 0.05 - 0.94, p < 0.001). Botanical origin strongly influenced honey color and ionic profiles, whereas geographical origin had a more limited effect possibly due to similarities among the sampled production areas. Pollen-based exploratory PCA clustered chestnut, acacia, and lavender honeys, mainly driven by Castanea pollen. In contrast, PCA showed no clear geographical clustering based on pollen or physicochemical data. These results suggest that combining palynological and chemical profiles can help characterize botanical origin, while geographical discrimination requires further investigation using larger and more balanced datasets.

food.title: Effect of enrichment, stocking density and breed on feather corticosterone, feather dehydroepiandrosterone (sulphate) and their ratio in broiler chickens
food.abstract: 1. Understanding how husbandry practices affect chronic stress in broiler chickens is crucial to improve animal welfare.2. This study examined the separate and combined effects of environmental enrichment, stocking density and breed on feather corticosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone (sulphate) (DHEA(S)). These are two endocrine indicators of (long-term) stress.3. In four separate 2⨯2 factorial design experiments in Poland and two separate 2⨯2 factorial design experiments in the Netherlands, broilers with different growth rates were reared under different housing conditions. These varied in enrichment types and stocking densities, representing both conventional and less intensive conditions.4. Feather corticosterone concentrations were elevated in broilers housed without environmental enrichment and/or at higher stocking densities. However, feather corticosterone was not elevated in the faster growing breeds, but rather was lower or there was no genotype effect. The effects of enrichment, stocking density, breed and their interactions were less clear for feather DHEA(S) patterns and the corticosterone/DHEA(S) ratio.5. The results suggested that, while enrichment and stocking density clearly affected stress, the role of DHEA(S) remains complex and poorly understood.6. Further research is needed to confirm if DHEA(S) in feathers is a reliable biomarker of chronic stress in broiler chickens.

food.title: Species-dependent differences in aquaporin immunoreactivity in avian brain tissues
food.abstract: 1. Aquaporins are membrane water channel proteins that regulate cellular water transport while maintaining electrochemical gradients across cell membranes. This study investigated the expression patterns of aquaporins 1, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 11 brain tissues of Alectoris chukar, Coturnix coturnix and Gallus gallus domesticus using immunohistochemical and Western blot analyses. Astrocytic involvement was evaluated through Glial fibrillary acidic protein immunoreactivity.2. All examined Aquaporins were expressed in the brain tissues of all species, with clear species-dependent differences in expression intensity and distribution patterns. Aquaporin immunoreactivity was predominantly associated with vascular and perivascular structures across all species.3. Glial fibrillary acidic protein immunoreactivity showed a species-dependent pattern, indicating variability in astrocytic density and reactivity among the studied avian brains. The highest astrocytic involvement was observed in G. gallus domesticus, followed by A. chukar, while C. coturnix exhibited comparatively lower astrocytic reactivity. No sex-related differences were observed, which suggested that astrocytic distribution is primarily species-dependent rather than sex-dependent.4. These results showed a coordinated relationship between aquaporin expression and astrocytic architecture in the regulation of brain waterhomoeostasis. The species-specific differences reflected functional adaptations in avian neurovascular and astroglial systems.

food.title: Characterization of the metabolic plasticity of Oenococcus oeni strains as a function of the oenological matrix by untargeted exometabolomic profiling
food.abstract: Malolactic fermentation (MLF), predominantly executed by the lactic acid bacterium Oenococcus oeni, constitutes a critical process that converts L-malic acid into L-lactic acid, contributing to the microbiological stability and sensory properties of the wine. The substantial functional and genetic diversity of O. oeni gives rise to considerable metabolic heterogeneity. The objective of this study was to characterize the metabolic plasticity of eight strains of O. oeni inoculated into four red wine matrices. An analysis was conducted on the wines of Pinot Noir and Merlot, analyzed in both adjusted and unadjusted forms in terms of pH and L-malic acid concentration. To achieve this objective, we combined the monitoring of L-malic acid consumption with untargeted metabolomic profiling (LC-MS). Exometabolomic analysis enabled the mapping of metabolic variability. Although a common metabolic basis, oriented towards survival functions, was observed, distinct metabolic profiles suggest different adaptive strategies emerged between strains, particularly in the potential mobilization of central pathways and in membrane regulation or flavonoid degradation. Furthermore, oenological adjustments, regulated metabolic expression, and the nature of the matrix strongly influence the response. Polyphenols and derivatives constituted a significant proportion of the biomarkers up-regulated by all O. oeni strains. These results suggest the potential influence of the interaction between microbial genotype and wine composition on MLF outcomes. They reinforce the notion of functional plasticity in O. oeni, offering potential leverage for the customization of red wine profiles.

food.title: Interpretable discrimination of extra virgin olive oil adulteration using NIR and FTIR spectroscopy combined with PCA-SHAP analysis
food.abstract: Extra virgin olive oil (EVOO), a high-value product of the olive oil sub-sector, is vulnerable to economically motivated adulteration, creating a need for rapid and trustworthy quality-control tools across the agri-food chain. This study developed an interpretable spectroscopic strategy for distinguishing authentic EVOO from samples adulterated with sunflower oil, refined olive oil, and olive pomace oil. Near infrared (NIR) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra were reduced by principal component analysis (PCA) and modelled using six classifiers, including decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), support vector machine (SVM), and gradient boosting machine (GBM). Model performance was evaluated using a formulation-group-held-out prediction strategy within the controlled source oil system, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, dependence plots, loading profiles, and interaction analysis were used for interpretation. The NIR-based RF model achieved the best prediction accuracy of 0.982, outperforming the best FTIR-based model with 0.821. SHAP analysis showed that the NIR model mainly relied on PC1, PC3, and PC4, which captured subtle multivariate variations across lipid-related NIR regions, indicating that the strongest absorption peaks were not necessarily the most discriminative features. In contrast, the FTIR model relied mainly on PCs associated with common triglyceride bands shared across oil categories, providing less class-specific information and partly explaining its weaker discrimination. The proposed PCA-SHAP framework supports transparent and chemically interpretable AI-based authentication of olive-derived agricultural products.

food.title: Comparative evaluation of turbidity and impedance microbiology for rapid quantification of Bacillus cereus in skim milk under different temperatures, salt levels, and incubation times
food.abstract: Rapid quantification of Bacillus cereus in milk is critical because this organism can survive pasteurization, grow during chilled storage, and cause spoilage or foodborne illness. This study compares a microplate-based turbidimetric system (Bioscreen C o Pro™) with an automated impedance analyzer (BacTrac 4300) for enumerating B. cereus in skim milk across a factorial combination of four temperatures (10, 20, 30, and 37 °C), four sodium chloride levels (0.11, 0.8, 1.5, and 3.0% (w/v) NaCl), and two incubation times (24 and 72 h). Bacterial growth was monitored in parallel by plate counting, optical density at 600 nm (OD 600 nm ), and impedance measurements, and primary Baranyi–Roberts modeling was used to derive method-specific detection times (DTs). Method-specific calibration equations relating DTs to viable bacterial concentrations were established and subsequently used to estimate B. cereus populations in skim milk samples previously incubated under different temperature, salinity, and incubation time conditions. Both rapid methods showed strong linear relationships between DT and actual cell concentration (log 10 CFU/mL), but impedance-based predictions demonstrated better agreement with plate counts than turbidimetric predictions ( R 2 = 0.90 vs. 0.82; pooled RMSE = 0.657 vs. 1.153 log₁₀CFU/mL, respectively) and consistently yielded shorter DTs, particularly at higher temperatures and longer incubation times, while elevated NaCl and low temperature markedly delayed or prevented growth. These findings provide a systematic, plate-count-referenced comparison of turbidimetric and impedance-based quantification of B. cereus under the tested skim-milk conditions. food.title: Antifungal effect of Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 on postharvest internal decay of chestnut and its potential antifungal mechanisms
food.abstract: Chestnut Inner Rot Disease (CIRD), a serious postharvest disease caused by multiple fungal pathogens, leads to substantial economic losses in the chestnut industry. Microbial biocontrol offers a safe and effective strategy. In this study, targeting four dominant CIRD pathogenic strains previously isolated, a bacterial strain identified as Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 was isolated from chestnut-cultivated soil. BLS-7 exhibited strong antifungal activity against Diaporthe phaseolorum, Colletotrichum siamense, Fusarium culmorum, and Lasiodiplodia theobromae, with inhibition rates of 84.51% to 96.89%. Moreover, it demonstrated broad-spectrum antagonism against 14 tested pathogenic fungi, all with inhibition rates exceeding 64%. In vivo assays further verified the significant biocontrol efficacy of BLS-7 across different chestnut varieties. Whole-genome sequencing analysis revealed that the BLS-7 genome harbors 13 gene clusters associated with secondary metabolite synthesis. Through headspace solid-phase microextraction combined with Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) of BLS-7 were analyzed, identifying hexyl butyrate as a candidate key inhibitory monomer. This compound inhibited three of the four CIRD pathogens by over 80% in vitro and all four in chestnut assays, with maximum inhibition rates of 82.95% and 75.3%, respectively. Both the VOCs and hexyl butyrate produced by BLS-7 suppressed mycelial growth and sporulation by disrupting hyphal morphology. VOCs and hexyl butyrate also restricted fungal spread on chestnuts and delayed fruit quality deterioration. This work proposes a fumigation-mediated VOC strategy using hexyl butyrate as a candidate key effector against multi-pathogen chestnut rot, offering a promising…

food.title: Influences of dietary valine supplementation on performance, intestinal traits and expression of lipid metabolism-related genes in broilers
food.abstract: 1. In diets based on corn and soybean meal, valine (Val) is considered the fourth limiting amino acid. However, studies on how broilers respond to Val remain limited.2. A total of 336, 1-d-old broilers were assigned to one of three dietary treatments, comprising eight replicates of 14 birds. The diet treatments were valine at 0.97 (CON), 1.05 (Val1) and 1.10% (Val2), respectively.3. There was no effect on body weight (BW), average daily weight gain (ADWG) or average daily feed intake (ADFI) during the whole period; however, Val1 improved feed conversion ratio (FCR; p < 0.05). The Val level had no effect on serum biochemical parameters. Broilers in the Val 1 group had a higher relative weight of the ileum and relative length of the duodenum (p < 0.05). No significant differences in duodenal digestive enzyme activities were observed. The activity of α-amylase in the jejunum decreased in the Val1 group but jejunal trypsin showed an increased significance in Val2 (p < 0.05). Compared with the CON diet, hepatic C/EBPα, SREBP-1c, ACC and FAS gene expression were decreased in the Val1 group, while CPT1 expression increased (p < 0.05). In the Val2 group, the expression levels of PPARα and CPT1 genes were upregulated (p < 0.05), with no alterations in the remaining gene.4. In conclusion, higher dietary Val inclusion improved FCR and modulated intestinal development, jejunal digestive enzyme activities and hepatic lipid metabolism-related gene expression in broilers.
